brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn whether wearable motion sensors and video-based movement analysis can track changes in arm function over time in adults with neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome (NTOS) who are receiving standard treatment (physical therapy or surgery).

NTOS happens when nerves between the neck and shoulder are squeezed, causing pain, numbness, weakness, and trouble using the arm. There is currently no objective test to measure how severe NTOS is or how well treatment is working.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Can digital measurements of arm movement, collected with wearable sensors and with standard webcam video, detect changes in arm function after NTOS treatment?
* Are these digital measurements more sensitive to change than standard questionnaires?
* Do video-based measurements agree with sensor-based measurements?
* Can measurements taken before treatment help predict who will improve with physical therapy?

This study does not assign or change treatment. Physical therapy or surgery is chosen by each participant's doctors as part of usual care.

Participants will:

* Complete 5 study visits over about 12 months: before treatment and 1 and 2 months after treatment (in clinic), and 6 and 12 months after treatment (remote telemedicine visits)
* At each visit, perform a short arm movement task (the "Press Test," a 20-second hand-over-head exercise) while wearing motion sensors and/or being recorded on video
* Complete questionnaires about arm function, pain, mood, and overall health
conditions: Neurogenic Thoracic Outlet Syndrome Thoracic Outlet Syndrome
primary_outcomes: Change in Press Test Digital Biomarkers of Upper Extremity Function
Change in Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) Score
title: Wearable Sensors and Video-Based Testing to Track Arm Function After Treatment for Neurogenic Thoracic Outlet Syndrome

brief_summary: This observational study aims to examine how temperament, emotion regulation, and sport participation are related to global self-esteem in adolescents. Participants will complete questionnaires measuring temperament, cognitive reappraisal, expressive suppression, and global self-esteem. Information about sport participation, including participation status, sport type, weekly training hours, years of participation, and competition level, will also be collected. Demographic characteristics such as age and gender will be considered in the analyses. The researchers will use statistical and machine learning methods to determine how well these characteristics predict global self-esteem. The study will also examine whether nonlinear relationships and combinations of characteristics improve prediction compared with a standard linear model, and which characteristics contribute most strongly to prediction. Differences between adolescents who participate in sports and those who do not will also be explored. This study is observational. Participants will not be assigned to a sport program, treatment, or other intervention. Because the data will be collected at one point in time, the findings will describe associations and predictive relationships and will not establish cause and effect.
primary_outcomes: Global Self-Esteem
title: Adolescent Self-Esteem, Temperament, Emotion Regulation, and Sport Participation

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, multi-center, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial lasting 18 months. Participants will be randomized to 1:1 to Lithium Orotate or matching placebo. Double-blinding will be maintained for investigators, participants, and outcome assessors. An independent data monitoring committee will oversee safety. The study will utilize Lithium Orotate 5 mg twice daily. The U.S. Manufacturer is Nitricost. It is a synthetic, stable Lithium Salt. The Nutricost 5 mg capsules only contain Lithium Orotate. There is no Lithium Carbonate in the 5 mg product. The Lithium Carbonate is undesirable because it is sequestered in Amyloid Plaques. The Lithium Orotate has been shown to be resist degradation and sequestration by the Amyloid Plaques.

Recruitment is 6 months.

Treatment phase is 18 months. Follow up is 1 month for post treatment for safety.

Inclusion Criteria is adults aged 50-90 years; Diagnosis of probable Alzheimer's Disease (per NIA-AA criteria) or MCI (per Peterson criteria). Baseline MMSE score of 18-26 (for AD) or 24-30 (for MCI). Participants must be stable on approved AD medications (if applicable) for \>3 months. Participants must provide informed consent (or via legally authorized representative).

Exclusion Criteria includes: Severe renal impairment of eGFR \<40, or CKD III-IV, History of Bipolar disorder or other lithium contraindications, Concomitant use of medications interacting with Lithium (e.g., diuretics, NSAIDs), Significant comorbidities (e.g., uncontrolled hypertension, recent stroke), Pregnancy or breastfeeding,

The Risk Benefit Ratio is extremely low. 1/100. The relative risk of using Lithium Orotate is extremely small compared to the possible significant benefits. The FDA has cleared the use of Lithium Orotate in this clinical trial.

The Sample Size is 200 participants (100 per arm), powered to detect a 2-point difference in MMSE change (SD=4, a+-=0.05, power=80%, 20% attrition). Stratification by AD/MCI status and age.

The Active Arm is Lithium Orotate capsules 10 mg orally daily. The Placebo Arm is Identical placebo capsules daily. Dosing of Lithium Orotate will be titrated down to 5 mg QD, if needed for tolerability. Compliance will be assessed via pill counts and patient diaries.

The Primary Endpoint is change in MMSE score from baseline, assessed every 3 months. Secondary Endpoint is PET Scan changes of Amyloid burden and/or Tau pathology at baseline and 18 months. PET Scans are optional only for participants that have an allergy to the PET Scan radionuclide, or have significant difficulty in transfers or transports to the imaging facility. Some participants will likely be home bound and unable to comply.

Safety and Incidence of adverse events (AEs), serious AEs and discontinuations will be monitored via common terminology criteria for adverse events (CTCAE).

Tolerability will be monitored via vital signs, renal functions (eGFR), thyroid function (TSH) and electrolyte panels every 3 months.
primary_outcomes: 2 Point change in MMSE Scores. Clock Drawing Tests change pass to fail or vice versa.
title: A Prospective, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Double Blind, 18 Month Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Tolerability of Lithium Orotate 10 mg Daily in Patients With Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment.

brief_summary:
This study evaluates whether a 12-month supervised progressive resistance training program improves lean body mass and metabolic health in obese North Indian adults aged 35-60 years. Asian Indians are uniquely predisposed to sarcopenic obesity-the coexistence of excess body fat and reduced muscle mass-which significantly increases the risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

Participants will be stratified into High-Ratio and Low-Ratio groups based on their baseline Myostatin/Follistatin (MSTN/FST) ratio, an biological index of muscle catabolism versus growth. Half of the participants in each stratum will undergo a 12-month supervised resistance training program, while the other half will receive standard lifestyle advice. The primary goal is to determine whether baseline MSTN/FST ratio predicts the extent of muscle mass gain and whether reducing this ratio mediates improvements in insulin resistance and systemic inflammation.

Participants will be randomly assigned to undergo germectomy using either the lateral trepanation approach or the conventional crestal osteotomy approach. Postoperative clinical recovery (such as pain, swelling, and trismus) and radiographic bone healing will be evaluated and compared between both groups.

brief_summary:
This pilot study investigates a new approach for patients with metastatic cancer that has spread to the brain (brain metastases) who are already planned to receive both fractionated stereotactic radiosurgery (fSRS) and brain surgery as standard treatment for their condition. Usually, surgery comes first, followed by radiation. However, post-operative radiation can sometimes lead to the cancer returning in the area, spreading to the brain's lining (LMD), or causing side effects from radiation (RN). This study hypothesizes that delivering fSRS before surgery may improve outcomes by enabling more accurate targeting, reducing tumor spillage, and potentially decreasing RN, while improving treatment compliance. The study is specifically testing the sequence of these two standard treatments.

This is a single-arm, prospective study enrolling 12 adult participants (age \>18) with 1-5 brain metastases, where one main tumor (between 2.0-5.0 cm diameter) requires surgical resection. Participants will receive fSRS (27 Gy in 3 fractions) approximately one week prior to surgery, as part of the study's approach. Throughout the study, participants will also have regular brain MRI scans to monitor their condition and complete tests to check memory and thinking skills (like the MoCA test) at various points.

The main goal is to see how well the cancer is controlled at the surgery site (called local freedom from progression, or FFP) over 6, 12, 18, and 24 months post-operatively. Secondary outcomes include rates of LMD and RN. Safety (adverse events, toxicities) will be continuously monitored by an independent Data Safety Monitoring Committee (DSMC). Each participant will be in the study for 2 years.

This research aims to provide preliminary data to inform future larger, randomized trials, ultimately improving treatment strategies for patients with metastatic brain cancer.
primary_outcomes: Local Freedom from Progression (FFP) within the Resection Cavity
title: Pre-Operative fSRS for Brain Metastases

brief_summary:
The ASA Physical Status Classification is widely used in preoperative risk assessment, but agreement between raters is limited, particularly between ASA II and III. This prospective observational study compares the ASA class assigned to the same patients by three types of raters: anesthesia residents working in the preoperative anesthesia clinic, a large language model (LLM), and a consensus of two senior anesthesiologists, which is the reference standard.

Residents complete the standard preoperative evaluation form and assign an ASA class as part of routine care. A copy of the completed form, with patient identifiers and the resident's ASA class removed, is then given independently to the LLM and to the two senior anesthesiologists. No intervention is applied to participants and routine care is not changed.

The primary aim is to measure how closely the residents and the LLM agree with the expert consensus (weighted kappa). Secondary aims are agreement among all three raters, agreement between the two senior anesthesiologists, the direction of misclassification, and how often the LLM matches the consensus when the resident does not.
primary_outcomes: Agreement between resident and expert-consensus ASA classification (quadratic weighted kappa)
Agreement between large language model and expert-consensus ASA classification (quadratic weighted kappa)
title: Agreement of ASA Physical Status Classification Among Anesthesia Residents, a Large Language Model, and Senior Anesthesiologist Consensus

Participants will be assigned to different dose groups. This study consists of two parts, namely the dose escalation stage and the dose expansion stage. brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare the effectiveness of epidural analgesia and the pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block in managing postoperative pain after total hip replacement surgery in adults. The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Does PENG block provide better pain relief than epidural analgesia? Which method results in fewer complications and side effects? How do both pain management techniques affect mobility and recovery time? Researchers will compare epidural analgesia with PENG block to determine which method provides better pain control, fewer side effects, and improved patient recovery.

Participants will:

Receive either epidural analgesia or PENG block after hip replacement surgery. Have their pain levels monitored at regular time points. Be assessed for mobility, complications, and overall satisfaction. This study aims to help doctors find the best pain management option for hip replacement patients, improving comfort, mobility, and recovery outcomes.

Epidural Analgesia with Continuous Bupivacaine Infusion
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity
title: Postoperative Pain Management in Hip Arthroplasty: Comparing Epidural Analgesia and PENG Block

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare two different treatment methods for physiological gingival hyperpigmentation (dark gums): conventional surgical depigmentation using the scalpel technique and intramucosal injection of glutathione.

A total of 32 adult participants with gingival hyperpigmentation will be randomly allocated into two groups. The first group will receive conventional scalpel depigmentation, while the second group will receive intramucosal glutathione injections.

The effectiveness of both treatment methods will be evaluated by measuring gingival pigmentation using the Dummett Oral Pigmentation Index (DOPI) and Hedin Melanin Index. Pain intensity, postoperative bleeding, wound healing, and histopathological changes will also be assessed during follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Change in Gingival Melanin Area Fraction From Baseline to 6 Months
title: Glutathione Injections Compared With Scalpel Treatment for Dark Gums

brief_summary: XenCART is an autologous bispecific CD20 and CD19 CAR T cell product from Cellogen Therapeutics Pvt Ltd. This first in human Phase I study at CMC Vellore will evaluate its safety tolerability and preliminary efficacy in adults with relapsed or refractory CD19 and CD20 positive B cell malignancies including B NHL and B ALL. Patients will undergo leukapheresis 9 to 12 day manufacturing fludarabine and cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion and a single intravenous infusion. The study includes a 28 day DLT evaluation period 24 months of active follow up and long term follow up thereafter. A 3 plus 3 dose escalation design with DSMB review after each cohort will evaluate sequential dose levels of 1 2 and 4 x 10 to the power 6 CAR T cells per kg to determine the recommended Phase II dose. Dual antigen targeting is expected to reduce CD19 negative relapse which is a major limitation of single target CAR T therapy. The study will establish the safety profile of XenCART and support its further development in India.

brief_summary: Thoracic aortic surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is one of the most invasive procedures in cardiac surgery. It often requires prolonged CPB and aortic cross-clamp times, and sometimes hypothermic circulatory arrest with selective cerebral perfusion. Multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) is a leading cause of death and prolonged intensive care unit (ICU) stay after these operations. However, most studies have examined single organ complications, such as acute kidney injury or respiratory failure, and data on MODS as a whole remain limited, particularly in Vietnam. This retrospective cohort study will review the medical records of adult patients who underwent thoracic aortic surgery with CPB at Hanoi Medical University Hospital from September 2019 to September 2026. Organ function will be assessed daily with the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score from ICU admission until ICU discharge. The study aims to describe the clinical and paraclinical characteristics of these patients, to determine the incidence of postoperative MODS, and to identify preoperative and intraoperative factors associated with MODS.
interventions: Thoracic aortic surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass
primary_outcomes: Incidence of postoperative multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS)
title: Multiple Organ Dysfunction After Thoracic Aortic Surgery With Cardiopulmonary Bypass

brief_summary:
Bleeding disorder of unknown cause (BDUC) affects people who experience excessive bleeding despite normal routine laboratory tests. Undetected platelet dysfunction may contribute to their bleeding symptoms.

The TARGET-BDUC study aims to investigate platelet function, particularly the formation of procoagulant platelets, and identify underlying mechanisms and potential diagnostic biomarkers.

The study will include 100 patients with BDUC and 30 healthy controls. Advanced platelet function testing, imaging, and proteomic and lipidomic analyses will be performed.

The findings may improve the diagnosis of BDUC and help identify patients who could benefit from targeted treatment.
primary_outcomes: Procoagulant Platelet Formation in Patients With BDUC Compared With Healthy Controls
title: Platelet Dysfunction in Patients With Bleeding Disorder of Unknown Cause

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if combining pregabalin and ibuprofen, given before surgery (preemptive analgesia), works to reduce pain after spine surgery in adults aged 18-60 years. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the combination of pregabalin and ibuprofen lower postoperative pain scores (VAS) over the first 24 hours after surgery? Does it lengthen the time until a patient first needs additional pain relief (morphine through a patient-controlled analgesia, or PCA, device)? Does it reduce the total amount of additional morphine needed in 24 hours? Does it shorten the length of hospital stay?

Researchers will compare the combination of pregabalin and ibuprofen to a control (a sugar capsule and 0.9% saline, which contain no active drug) to see if the combination works to treat pain after spine surgery. All participants will also receive the standard pain medicines paracetamol and ketorolac.

Participants will:

Take pregabalin 150 mg by mouth 2 hours before surgery and receive ibuprofen 400 mg by vein 30 minutes before anesthesia induction, or take a sugar capsule and receive 0.9% saline at the same times Undergo elective spine surgery under general anesthesia Use a PCA morphine device after waking from anesthesia whenever they feel pain (VAS above 4) Rate their pain on a visual analogue scale (VAS) at hours 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, and 24 after surgery Be followed until hospital discharge
primary_outcomes: Postoperative pain score (Visual Analogue Scale)
Time to first additional analgesia (minutes from extubation to first PCA morphine press)
Total additional analgesia (cumulative PCA morphine dose, mg)
Length of hospital stay (days from end of surgery to discharge)
Incidence of significant pain (VAS > 3 at any time point)
title: Comparison of Ibuprofen and Pregabalin With Control as Preemptive Analgesia in Spine Surgery

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate changes in salivary antioxidant capacity, oxidative stress biomarkers, and self-perceived general well-being during eight weeks of postbiotic supplementation in generally healthy adults.

Thirty-six participants aged 18 years or older will receive MettaBion Liquid twice daily for eight weeks. Assessments will be conducted before supplementation and at Weeks 4 and 8. Saliva samples will be analysed for total antioxidant capacity, malondialdehyde, 3-nitrotyrosine, and 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine. General well-being will be assessed using a visual analogue scale.

This prospective, single-arm study will estimate within-participant changes and their variability to inform the design and sample-size planning of a future randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
primary_outcomes: Change in salivary total antioxidant capacity from baseline to Week 8
title: Efficacy of Postbiotic Supplementation in Improving Antioxidant Status

brief_summary: This is a multicenter prospective observational cohort study with a nested physiological substudy. It aims to enroll 220 adults with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) initiating mask noninvasive ventilation (NIV). The study will assess the measurement feasibility, physiological associations, and early prognostic discrimination of the electrical impedance tomography (EIT)-derived flow index (EFI) during NIV. The primary objective is to estimate how well pre-landmark T1 EFI discriminates the risk of endotracheal intubation or all-cause death through 48 hours. A nested physiological substudy (n=20) will evaluate the within-patient association between EFI and airway occlusion pressure across fixed pressure support (PS) levels (5, 10, and 15 cmH2O). Clinical management remains independent of study measurements.
interventions: Brief Pressure Support Adjustment and Airway Occlusion (Substudy only)

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of psychosocial skills training on self-stigma and forgiveness among family caregivers of individuals with psychotic disorders. Caring for a person with a long-term mental illness can create emotional and social challenges. Family caregivers may experience stigma, difficulties in social relationships, and challenges related to forgiveness.

The study will include 34 adult caregivers who will be randomly assigned to an intervention group (n=17) or a control group (n=17). The intervention group will receive an eight-session, face-to-face psychosocial skills training program delivered once a week. The program will focus on understanding mental illness, improving communication and problem-solving skills, supporting treatment, managing persistent symptoms, coping with stress, and strengthening social functioning. The control group will not receive the training during the study period.

Self-stigma and forgiveness will be assessed in both groups before the intervention, immediately after the eight-session program, and three months after the intervention. The findings will help determine whether psychosocial skills training can reduce self-stigma and improve forgiveness among caregivers of individuals with psychotic disorders.
primary_outcomes: Change in Caregiver Self-Stigma
Change in Caregiver Forgiveness
title: Effects of Psychosocial Skills Training on Self-Stigma and Forgiveness Among Caregivers of Individuals With Psychotic Disorders

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine the impact of process and formulation on glycemic index (GI) of bread, whether consumed on its own or as part of a meal, in healthy volunteers.

Two types of bread are compared to a reference one. The two types of bread are:

* a part-baked bread
* a part-baked bread enriched with a polyphenols-rich sugarcane extract

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Do part-baking or the combination of part-baking and polyphenols addition allow GI reduction of breads when they are consumed alone?
* Do part-baking or the combination of part-baking and polyphenols addition reduce postprandial glycemia when breads are consumed during a meal?
* For one type of bread, how food combination has impacted postprandial glycemia?
* Do part-baking or the combination of part-baking and polyphenols addition modify satiety?

Participants will:

* be equipped with commercial continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices to track interstitial glucose
* need to attend the laboratory for 9 days on a fasting state
* have to consume one of these items:
* glucose solution (3 days)
* bread alone (3 days = 1 day per type of bread)
* a meal containing a tomato soup, a sandwich made with bread (3 days = 1 day per type of bread), ham and cheese and an apple puree

After consumption, participants will:

* have to stay in the laboratory for 2 hours
* fill a form to evaluate their satiety
lead_sponsor: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement
primary_outcomes: Incremental Area Under the Interstitial Glucose Curve (iAUC)
title: Impact of Food Combination in a Meal on Nutrient Bioavailability and the Glycemic Index

brief_summary: This randomized quality improvement study will evaluate whether pop-up alerts in the electronic health record (EHR) increase prescribing of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) medications and continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) for eligible patients with diabetes. The study will be conducted at nine Montefiore Medical Group primary care sites. Primary care providers will be randomly assigned to either receive the alerts or not receive them. The alerts will remind providers that a patient is eligible for a GLP-1 RA, a CGM, or both, and will help them choose the option covered by the patient's insurance. Providers in both groups will use their own clinical judgment in deciding whether to prescribe. The study will use information already recorded in patients' medical records.

Percentage of Eligible Patients Newly Prescribed a CGM
title: EHR Alerts to Improve GLP-1 Medication and Continuous Glucose Monitor Prescribing in Primary Care

brief_summary:
KDTV001 Injection is a non-replicating adenovirus serotype 5 (Ad5)-based therapeutic HPV vaccine developed by Wuhan KadGeno Biotechnology Co., Ltd. It utilizes an engineered adenoviral vector expressing the HPV16/18/52 E6/E7 fusion protein under CMV promoter control, designed to inducing a robust cellular immune response that eradicates HPV-related lesions.

This is a Phase I, multicenter, open-label, dose-escalation and expansion study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, immunogenicity, and preliminary efficacy of KDTV001 Injection in participants with HPV types 16, and/or 18, and/or 52-associated cervical HSIL.

The study consists of three parts: dose escalation, an immunogenicity expansion cohort (Phase 1), and a dose expansion phase (Phase 2). In Phase 1a, 3+3 dose escalation of KDTV001 Injection will be conducted separately for IM and IC administration, with two ascending dose levels evaluated for each route. During the dose-escalation phase, if a dose cohort is assessed as safe by SRC, an immunogenicity expansion of 10-20 participants may be conducted. Based on Phase 1 safety and immunogenicity data, 1-2 dose levels will be selected for Phase 2 dose expansion for both IC and IM. In the Phase 2 dose-expansion phase, each dose cohort will enroll 30-50 participants. Both phases will consist of a screening period, a treatment and safety follow-up period, an end of study visit (EOS) and a long-term follow-up period.
conditions: Cervical High Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion
primary_outcomes: Phase 1: Incidence of Any Adverse Events (AEs), Treatment related AEs (TRAEs) and Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) Following Investigational Treatment for the Duration of the Study
Phase 2: Percentage of Participants With No Evidence of Cervical HSIL on Histology and No Evidence of HPV-16 and HPV-18 and HPV-52 in Cervical Samples
title: KDTV001 Injection in Patients With Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Types 16, and/or 18, and/or 52 Associated Cervical High-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion .

brief_summary:
The goal of this study was to learn whether virtual reality could reduce pain and improve comfort during shock wave treatment for urinary tract stones. This treatment is called extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL). It uses shock waves from outside the body to break stones into smaller pieces.

The main questions were:

* Did participants who used virtual reality report less pain than those who received usual care alone?
* Did participants who used virtual reality feel more comfortable?
* Did virtual reality affect vital signs, such as heart rate and blood pressure? The study included 65 adults aged 18 years or older who underwent their first ESWL treatment at Burdur State Hospital in Türkiye.

Participants were assigned by chance to one of two groups. One group used a virtual reality headset to watch a nature-themed video with sound during treatment. This group also received usual care. The other group received usual care without virtual reality.

Participants in both groups rated their pain and comfort from 0 to 10 before and after treatment. The research team also measured their vital signs at these times.

The study compared these measures between the two groups to assess the effects of adding virtual reality to usual care.
primary_outcomes: Pain Intensity
title: Virtual Reality for Pain and Comfort During ESWL for Urinary Tract Stones

brief_summary:
This clinical trial will compare two types of surgery for endometriosis affecting the rectum, the lower part of the bowel. It will include 200 women aged 18 to 45 years who have symptoms and a single area of rectal endometriosis smaller than 5 cm. All participants must need surgery and be suitable for either procedure.

The main questions are:

Do the two procedures differ in the risk of bowel complications within 90 days after surgery?

How do the procedures affect bowel function, quality of life, and pain?

Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups:

Discoid or double discoid excision: The surgeon removes one or two overlapping discs of the affected bowel wall without removing an entire bowel segment.

Segmental resection: The surgeon removes the affected bowel segment and joins the remaining bowel ends.

Both procedures will be performed using keyhole surgery. Assignment will take place during surgery, after the surgeon confirms that either procedure is suitable.

Researchers will compare bowel complications, including leakage from the bowel closure, narrowing of the rectum, and abnormal connections between the bowel and nearby organs or tissues. Participants will complete questionnaires about quality of life and bowel function before surgery and at 6 and 12 months afterward. Researchers will also assess pain, recovery, and the need for further surgery. Follow-up will continue for up to 24 months to assess later symptoms and further treatment.
interventions: Laparoscopic Discoid or Double Discoid Excision
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Major Bowel-Related Complications

Early postoperative outcomes were assessed on days 1, 3, and 7, with preoperative measurements obtained where applicable. Periodontal parameters of the adjacent mandibular second molar were assessed before surgery and eight weeks postoperatively.

This retrospective clinical study aims to evaluate the accuracy of full-arch dental implant placement in patients with terminal mandibular dentition using two different computer-guided surgical approaches.

Patients with terminal mandibular dentition often require extraction of their remaining teeth and placement of multiple dental implants to support a fixed full-arch prosthesis. Accurate implant placement is important for achieving a favorable prosthetic outcome and avoiding anatomical complications.

The study will compare two surgical workflows. The first uses a stackable surgical guide system in patients who require reduction of the jawbone to create adequate space for the final prosthesis. The second uses sequential tooth-supported surgical guides in patients who do not require bone reduction. These guides are used in stages during tooth extraction and implant placement to help transfer the digitally planned implant positions to the patient's jaw.

The researchers will review the clinical records, original digital treatment plans, and radiographic images of previously treated patients at the Faculty of Dentistry, Menoufia University. Patients treated between 2024 and 2026 who meet the study eligibility criteria will be considered.

The accuracy of implant placement will be assessed by comparing the planned implant positions with the actual positions identified from postoperative three-dimensional imaging. The researchers will measure differences at the implant platform and tip, as well as differences in implant angulation.

The study aims to determine whether the two guided surgical workflows differ in implant placement accuracy and to provide clinical information that may help clinicians select an appropriate guided surgical approach for patients requiring mandibular full-arch implant rehabilitation.

Occupational therapy remains underutilised in oncology, despite its potential to help patients maintain or regain independence in meaningful daily activities. Collaboration between Advanced Practice Nurses and occupational therapists could improve the identification and management of occupational difficulties associated with CIPN.

brief_summary: Extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) is a key component of the Mediterranean diet and is widely recognized for its beneficial health effects, largely attributed to its high content of bioactive compounds such as polyphenols and monounsaturated fatty acids. However, in real-life conditions, olive oil is frequently consumed after culinary processing (e.g., frying, baking), which may alter its chemical composition and biological properties. In contrast, regular olive oil (OO) undergoes industrial processing that reduces its content of bioactive compounds and may generate potentially harmful substances. Despite increasing evidence supporting the health benefits of EVOO, there is a lack of clinical studies evaluating how culinary processing influences the metabolic response to different types of olive oil in humans. Furthermore, no specific metabolic biomarkers are currently available to distinguish the intake of thermally processed EVOO versus OO. Therefore, this study aims to identify and validate a distinctive metabolic fingerprint associated with the consumption of EVOO and OO after cooking, using a randomized, controlled, crossover, dose-response clinical trial in healthy adults. The findings will contribute to a better understanding of the health implications of culinary practices involving olive oil and support evidence-based dietary recommendations.

brief_summary:
BACKGROUND Biases toward certain groups of patients (weight bias, ageism, racism, ableism and sexism) are common among health professionals and can affect the quality and equity of care. Traditional teaching formats such as lectures have difficulty engaging medical students on these deeply rooted attitudes. "Augusta's Oath" (original French title: "Le Serment d'Augusta") is a 16-episode narrative educational podcast (about 60 minutes per episode) produced by the Faculty of Health of Sorbonne University (Paris, France). Combining care stories, patient testimonies and insights from the humanities, it is used in an elective teaching unit to encourage reflection and change how future physicians approach patients. A previous uncontrolled study suggested that listening to the podcast prompted changes in perspective among medical students, but its specific effect on biases has never been tested in a controlled trial with validated measures.

OBJECTIVE To assess whether listening to targeted podcast episodes, combined with reflective writing, specifically reduces five types of bias: weight bias, ageism, racism, ableism and sexism.

METHODS This is a randomized controlled trial with two parallel groups, offered to medical students enrolled in the podcast teaching unit at Sorbonne University. About 500 students who agree to take part in the research are randomly assigned (1:1, balanced by sex and year of study) to one of two listening programmes of 8 episodes each (about 8 hours of listening), with a short written reflection after each episode.

* Group A listens to episodes on weight bias, racism and sexual and gender-based violence, plus control episodes that do not address the biases measured.
* Group B listens to episodes on disability and ageism, plus a different set of control episodes.

Each group therefore serves as the comparison group for the biases addressed only in the other group ("mirror" design). Participants commit not to listen to the other group's episodes until they have completed the study questionnaires.

At the end of the listening programme, participants complete attitude questionnaires once: AFA and ATOP (weight bias), ATIBI (recognition of implicit racial bias), AMMSA (acceptance of myths about sexual aggression), UCLA-GAS-F (attitudes toward older adults) and the revised ATPD (attitudes toward people with disabilities). Scores are compared between the two groups.

Participation in the research is voluntary and has no effect on course validation: students who decline follow the same teaching unit without any data collection. Data are pseudonymized, and participants who complete all questionnaires receive compensation for the time spent on research tasks.

EXPECTED RESULTS The investigators expect each group to show more favourable attitudes than the other group specifically on the biases addressed by its own episodes. Positive results would support the wider use of this narrative podcast as a teaching tool in other French-speaking medical schools.
primary_outcomes: Composite Bias Score: Global Aligned Standardized Between-Group Effect Across Five Bias Scales
title: Effect of a Narrative Educational Podcast on Stereotypes and Prejudice Among Medical Students

This study will compare lumateperone monotherapy with usual antidepressant treatment in adults experiencing their first lifetime episode of major depressive disorder. Use of lumateperone alone for this form of depression is investigational.

The study will enroll 134 adults aged 18 to 65 years who have clinically significant depression and have not received medication to treat their current depressive episode. Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups. One group will receive lumateperone 42 mg once daily as the only scheduled medicine used to treat depression. The other group will receive sertraline or escitalopram, selected by the treating psychiatrist. Treatment will last eight weeks.

Both groups will receive the same scheduled clinical contacts, information about depression, and access to psychological care. A trained assessor who does not know the assigned treatment will measure depressive symptoms at the beginning of the study and after 2, 4, and 8 weeks.

The main outcome will be improvement in depressive symptoms at week 8. Other outcomes will include response, remission, unwanted effects, stopping medication because of unwanted effects, and the need to switch or add another depression treatment. There will be weekly contact during treatment and a safety follow-up at week 10. Treatment may be changed at any time when clinically necessary. Recruitment will begin only after the required ethics and regulatory approvals have been obtained.

brief_summary: Sarcopenia is a common complication of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and resistance exercise is the main recommended treatment. Patients with sarcopenia who were eligible for exercise were randomized into two groups for 12 weeks: resistance exercise alone, or resistance exercise plus brisk walking. brief_summary:
Climate change poses significant risks to maternal, fetal, and neonatal health through environmental hazards such as extreme heat, air pollution, and climate-related disasters. Midwives play a crucial role in identifying these risks, providing preventive counseling, and promoting climate-resilient perinatal care. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI)-supported simulation into midwifery education may enhance students' knowledge, climate change awareness, and clinical risk assessment skills.

This study aims to evaluate the effect of climate-resilient perinatal care training supported by an AI-powered chatbot simulator on midwifery students' climate change knowledge, awareness, and climate-related perinatal risk assessment skills.

The study is designed as a randomized controlled trial with pretest, posttest, and four-week follow-up assessments. A total of 88 third- and fourth-year midwifery students at the University of Health Sciences, Hamidiye Faculty of Health Sciences, Türkiye, will be allocated to an intervention group (n=44) or a control group (n=44) using stratified randomization based on academic year and grade point average.

Both groups will receive a four-week climate-resilient perinatal care education program consisting of eight hours of face-to-face training. Following the educational program, the intervention group will participate in AI-powered chatbot-based clinical simulations involving climate-related perinatal health scenarios, while the control group will receive an educational brochure.

Climate-resilient perinatal care knowledge and climate change awareness will be assessed in both groups at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and at a four-week follow-up. Climate-related perinatal risk assessment skills will additionally be evaluated in the intervention group at posttest and follow-up using a structured observational assessment tool.

The findings are expected to provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of AI-supported simulation in climate-resilient midwifery education.
primary_outcomes: Climate-Resilient Perinatal Care Knowledge Score
Climate Change Awareness Score
Climate-Related Perinatal Risk Assessment Skills Score
title: The Effect of AI-Powered Chatbot Simulator-Based Climate-Resilient Perinatal Care Training on Midwifery Students' Climate Change Knowledge, Awareness, and Risk Assessment Skills

brief_summary:
This observational study aimed to investigate how external training load varies between professional football players and across training sessions during an 11-week preparation period.

Monitoring training load is important for understanding the physical demands placed on athletes and supporting effective training planning. Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS/GPS) devices allow sports scientists and coaches to measure how far players run, how fast they move, and other physical demands experienced during training. However, it remains unclear how much of the variation in these measurements is related to individual players compared with the training sessions they attend.

The study included 17 professional football players from one team who were monitored during 53 regular training sessions over 11 weeks. Players followed their usual team training program, which included football-specific technical and tactical activities and physical conditioning. No additional training intervention was assigned by the researchers.

External training load was assessed using wearable GNSS/GPS devices. The measurements included total distance covered, distance covered at different running speeds, maximum running speed, high metabolic load distance, acceleration and deceleration counts, and device-derived training load.

The primary objective was to examine differences in total distance covered during training and determine how much variability could be attributed to individual players and shared training sessions. Secondary objectives included examining other external training load measurements and evaluating whether these measurements differed across the 11-week preparation period.

The collected data were analyzed using statistical methods that accounted for repeated measurements from the same players and observations shared within training sessions.

This study may help sports scientists, coaches, and performance practitioners better understand GNSS/GPS training data and support more informed decisions about monitoring physical demands in professional football.
primary_outcomes: Total Distance Covered During Training (m)
title: This Observational Study Investigated Player- and Training-session-level Variability in GNSS-derived External Training Load During an 11-week Preparation Period in Professional Football. Seventeen Professional Players Were Monitored Across 53 Team Training Sessions. External Load Variables Included.

Postoperative cognitive complaints are common among older adults undergoing cardiac surgery and may negatively affect recovery, daily functioning, independence, and quality of life. The ECPON II study evaluates the effectiveness of a co-designed, nurse navigator-led intervention designed to support cognitive and postoperative recovery in older adults undergoing cardiac surgery.

Fifty patients aged 65 years or older undergoing cardiac surgery will receive the intervention. Outcomes will be compared with data from 150 matched historical controls from the previous ECPON observational study (ECPON I; NCT06469515). The historical controls are not enrolled in ECPON II.

The intervention consists of four coordinated components: information and education, postoperative consultations, cognitive assessments, and peer support, coordinated and delivered by a nurse navigator. The primary outcome is patient-reported cognitive complaints. Secondary outcomes include postoperative recovery, cognitive function, delirium, frailty, depression, health-related quality of life, functional capacity, self-efficacy, caregiver burden, and cost-utility. brief_summary:
Chronic venous leg ulcers can be painful and prone to infection. They can significantly limit a patient's function, mobility and quality of life.

A major contributor to delayed ulcer healing is persistent bacteria. Treatments that can penetrate the bacteria's protective outer shield to kill and clear the bacteria are important for helping ulcers heal more quickly.

The purpose of this pilot study is to test a topical study treatment (called ClearToe Serum®) plus two types of light (red and blue-purple light) in the treatment of chronic venous ulcers.

This is an open-label single-arm pilot study. All participants will receive the test treatment as well as standard or care treatment for their chronic venous ulcer. Participants will receive study treatments one per week for up to 12 weeks, or until their ulcer is healed.

The main objectives are to assess adherence to the one-per-week study treatments, and to note any study device-related, study treatment-related, or serious adverse events, or adverse events that lead to stopping study treatment.

brief_summary:
Unilateral vestibular hypofunction (UVH) is a condition in which the balance system in one inner ear does not function properly. People with this condition may experience dizziness, blurred vision during head movements, difficulty maintaining balance, and problems walking, particularly when performing two tasks at the same time.

Vestibular rehabilitation is an exercise-based treatment designed to improve balance, gaze stability, and daily functioning. Dual-task training involves performing a physical activity while simultaneously completing a mental or another physical task, such as walking while counting backward.

The purpose of this study is to investigate whether combining dual-task training with vestibular rehabilitation is more effective than traditional vestibular rehabilitation alone in improving vestibular function, dizziness, balance, and walking ability in adults with unilateral vestibular hypofunction.

This study is a single-blind randomized controlled trial involving 50 adults aged 18 to 65 years with unilateral vestibular hypofunction. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The first group will receive traditional vestibular rehabilitation, while the second group will receive vestibular rehabilitation combined with dual-task training. Both groups will complete two treatment sessions per week for four weeks, for a total of eight sessions.

Participants will undergo assessments before and after the four-week intervention to evaluate vestibular function, dizziness-related disability, balance, walking ability, attention, and working memory. The findings may help determine whether adding dual-task training provides additional benefits for people with unilateral vestibular hypofunction.
interventions: Vestibular Rehabilitation Combined With Dual-Task Training
primary_outcomes: Change in Vestibulo-Ocular Reflex (VOR) Gain
Change in Vestibular Evoked Myogenic Potential (VEMP) Responses
title: Effect of Vestibular Rehabilitation Combined With Dual-Task Training in Patients With Unilateral Vestibular Hypofunction

brief_summary:
Medical adhesive-related skin injuries (MARSI) are skin injuries that can occur when medical tapes, dressings, or other adhesive products are applied or removed. Patients undergoing open-heart surgery are frequently exposed to these products during postoperative care. Factors such as fragile skin, swelling, changes in blood circulation, and repeated dressing changes may increase the risk of skin injury.

This multicenter prospective observational study aims to determine how frequently MARSI occurs in adult patients undergoing open-heart surgery and to identify demographic, clinical, and dressing-related factors associated with its development.

Patients receiving postoperative care in cardiovascular surgery intensive care units at two hospitals in Türkiye will be observed during routine clinical care. Researchers will assess skin condition during dressing changes and record the occurrence, type, location, and characteristics of MARSI. Patient characteristics, clinical conditions, adhesive products, and dressing practices will also be evaluated. The Braden Scale and COMHON Index will be used to assess skin-related risk factors.

No experimental treatment or additional invasive procedures will be performed. The findings may help healthcare professionals identify patients at greater risk of MARSI and improve preventive skin care practices following open-heart surgery.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Medical Adhesive-Related Skin Injury (MARSI)
title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Medical Adhesive-Related Skin Injuries in Patients Undergoing Open Heart Surgery

brief_summary: The MASA (Metabolic-Atrial-Septal-Assessment) score is a simple 0-8 point score built from five routinely available variables: estimated glomerular filtration rate, serum triglycerides, absence of atrial septal aneurysm, left atrial diameter, and TAPSE. In a retrospective development cohort (n=246), a score of 5 or more identified patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). This prospective study will test, in consecutive patients with cardiovascular disease or stroke without known AF admitted to the Intensive Care Unit, whether a MASA score of 5 or more identifies those in whom AF is detected by continuous ECG monitoring. The score, its threshold, and the primary outcome are fixed before enrollment and will not be changed.
lead_sponsor: Special Hospital for Cerebrovascular Diseases "Sveti Sava"
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity and Specificity of MASA Score >=5 for Detection of Atrial Fibrillation
title: Prospective Validation of the MASA Score for Detection of Previously Unknown Atrial Fibrillation

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn how often bile leaks after major liver surgery, which factors increase the risk of a leak, and whether simple bilirubin tests on the fluid collected by the surgical drain in the first days after the operation can predict a serious leak. The study will include adults having planned removal of three or more liver segments (major hepatectomy) for any reason at Minia University, Egypt.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How many patients develop a clinically relevant bile leak (one that needs a drainage procedure, an endoscopic procedure or a second operation) within 90 days after major hepatectomy?
* Which patient, liver and operation-related factors are linked to bile leak?
* Can the bilirubin level in the drain fluid, and its ratio to the blood bilirubin level, measured on days 1 and 3 after surgery, show which patients will develop a clinically relevant bile leak?

Participants are adults whose liver operation has already been planned as part of their regular medical care. Taking part does not change their operation or treatment. Participants will:

* Have their usual pre-operative tests, operative details and hospital course recorded.
* Have bilirubin measured in a small sample of the fluid collected by the abdominal drain placed at the end of the operation, together with a routine blood test, on days 1, 3 and 5 after surgery and later while the drain remains in place.
* Be seen daily in hospital and at clinic visits about 2 weeks, 6 weeks and 90 days after surgery.

The researchers expect that higher drain-fluid bilirubin and a higher drain-to-blood bilirubin ratio early after surgery will identify patients at risk of a clinically relevant leak. If so, these simple tests could help surgeons decide when a drain can be removed safely and when a patient needs early investigation.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Clinically Relevant (ISGLS Grade B or C) Bile Leak
title: Risk Factors and Early Predictors of Bile Leak After Major Liver Resection

brief_summary:
Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM) is a severe, immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system predominantly affecting the pediatric population. Although high-dose intravenous corticosteroids (such as methylprednisolone) represent standard first-line therapy, a subset of clinical cases fails to achieve adequate clinical response, carrying high risks of persistent neurological disability, neurodevelopmental sequelae, or fulminant deterioration.

This randomized, open-label trial evaluates the clinical efficacy, neuroimaging outcomes, and safety profile of intravenous cyclophosphamide pulse therapy compared with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) as a rescue modality in pediatric patients under 14 years of age with steroid-refractory ADEM. Eligible participants are allocated using a computer-based random number generator. Enrolled patients are prospectively monitored for neurological recovery, functional disability using the pediatric Liverpool Outcome Score (LOS), radiological resolution on neuroimaging (MRI), overall survival, and treatment-emergent adverse events.
primary_outcomes: Neurological Functional Outcome and Disability Assessment by Liverpool Outcome Score (LOS)
title: Efficacy and Safety of Cyclophosphamide in Pediatric Patients With Steroid-Refractory Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM)

brief_summary:
This study aims to develop and prospectively validate machine learning models for predicting hypotension following spinal anesthesia in pregnant women undergoing elective cesarean delivery. The study consists of two cohorts: a retrospective training cohort including at least 200 patients and an independent prospective validation cohort including 50 patients.

Three machine learning algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression) will be trained using preoperative demographic, anthropometric, and baseline hemodynamic variables, including age, body mass index, parity, gestational age, baseline systolic blood pressure, and baseline heart rate.

The primary outcome is post-spinal hypotension, defined as a decrease in systolic blood pressure of at least 20% from baseline and/or the requirement for vasopressor administration within the first 15 minutes after spinal anesthesia.

The best-performing model will be evaluated in the independent prospective cohort to assess its predictive performance in a real clinical setting.
primary_outcomes: Predictive Performance of Machine Learning Models for Post-Spinal Hypotension
title: Prediction of Post-Spinal Hypotension During Cesarean Delivery Using Machine Learning Algorithms

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the safety, distribution in normal organs, radiation dose, and diagnostic value of 18F-labeled somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2) antagonist PET/CT imaging. Healthy volunteers will undergo imaging to assess tracer distribution and radiation exposure. Patients with pathologically confirmed grade 1 or 2 neuroendocrine tumors will undergo SSTR2 antagonist and 18F-octreotide PET/CT within 1 week to compare tumor detection and tracer uptake. Selected patients will also receive succinylated gelatin or amino acids before antagonist imaging to assess their effects on kidney and tumor uptake. Imaging findings will be compared with pathological results, SSTR2 expression, and clinical follow-up data.
lead_sponsor: Cancer Institute and Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences
primary_outcomes: Lesion Detection Rates of SSTR2 Antagonist PET/CT Versus 18F-Octreotide PET/CT
title: Application of 18F-SSTR2 Antagonist PET/CT in Neuroendocrine Tumors

brief_summary: Gastric cancer (GC) is the fifth most common cancer and the fifth leading cause of cancer death worldwide, with 37% of new cases occurring in China. The Correa cascade describes the progression from normal gastric mucosa to chronic inflammation, atrophic gastritis, intestinal metaplasia, intraepithelial neoplasia, and ultimately gastric cancer. Confocal laser endomicroscopy (CLE) enables real-time in vivo "optical biopsy" of gastrointestinal mucosa at subcellular resolution. However, CLE requires a learning curve and interpretation is subject to inter-operator variability. An AI diagnostic system has been developed by Qilu Hospital of Shandong University in collaboration with Wuxi Hisky Medical Technology Co., Ltd. to improve diagnostic performance and assist less experienced endoscopists. This large-sample, prospective, multicenter study aims to evaluate the diagnostic performance of the CLE AI diagnostic system for the whole-chain diagnosis of the gastric cancer Correa cascade, using histopathological diagnosis as the gold standard.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of the CLE AI diagnostic system for the Correa cascade
Diagnostic sensitivity of the CLE AI diagnostic system for the Correa cascade
Diagnostic specificity of the CLE AI diagnostic system for the Correa cascade
title: AI-assisted CLE for Whole-Chain Diagnosis of the Correa Cascade of Gastric Cancer

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effects of an eight-week roller-skate-based proprioceptive training programme on static and dynamic plantar loading and postural control in young tennis players with chronic ankle instability (CAI).

Forty tennis players aged 9 to 12 years with CAI, confirmed using the Cumberland Ankle Instability Tool (CAIT), will be allocated to either an experimental group (EG) or a control group (CG). Participants in the EG will complete an eight-week roller-skate-based proprioceptive training programme alongside their habitual tennis training, whereas participants in the CG will continue their habitual tennis training alone.

Static and dynamic baropodometry as well as static stabilometry (unipodal and bipodal stance, and Romberg Quotient) will be assessed at baseline (Week 0) and within two weeks post-intervention (Weeks 9 to 10). Between-group differences over time will be analysed using a two-by-two mixed-model analysis of variance (ANOVA).
primary_outcomes: Static Postural Control: Center of Pressure (CoP) 95% Confidence Ellipse Area
Static Postural Control: Center of Pressure (CoP) Mean Velocity

Dynamic Plantar Loading: Dynamic Ellipse Surface Area
title: Roller-Skate Proprioceptive Training for Tennis Players With Ankle Instability "The ROLTEN (ROLler-skate Proprioceptive Training for TENnis Players)"

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate the relationship between dynamic lumbopelvic kinematics and postural stability in individuals with lumbar radiculopathy and to compare these findings with those of healthy individuals.

The study will include individuals diagnosed with lumbar radiculopathy and healthy participants. Video recordings of participants will be obtained during three functional tasks: forward bending, step-up, and sit-to-stand. The recorded videos will subsequently be analyzed using Kinovea software to assess lumbopelvic movement angles, including pelvic tilt angle, lumbar lordosis angle, and trunk inclination angle. Postural stability will be assessed separately using the TOGU balance assessment system.

The study will investigate the correlations between each kinematic variable and the TOGU Stability Index. Additionally, differences in dynamic lumbopelvic movement angles and postural stability between individuals with lumbar radiculopathy and healthy participants will be examined.

The findings may contribute to a better understanding of dynamic movement patterns and postural stability in individuals with lumbar radiculopathy.
primary_outcomes: Correlation Between Pelvic Tilt Angle and TOGU Stability Index
title: Movement Patterns and Balance in People With Lumbar Radiculopathy

brief_summary:
This study evaluated a suicide prevention gatekeeper training program for firefighters in Taiwan. The study compared firefighters from two fire departments. The training group (96 firefighters) received a 120-minute in-person session that combined classroom instruction with practice conversations using an AI-assisted virtual character on the Virti platform. The comparison group (91 firefighters) received a suicide prevention handbook for police officers, firefighters, and other first responders to read on their own.

Both groups completed a baseline questionnaire. The training group completed the posttest immediately after the session, and the comparison group completed the posttest one week after receiving the handbook. Both groups were asked to complete a follow-up questionnaire at one month. The questionnaires assessed suicide prevention knowledge, confidence in helping someone at risk of suicide, psychological distress, and ability to cope with stress.

brief_summary:
Sarcopenia is an age-related condition characterized by a progressive loss of muscle mass, muscle strength, and physical performance. Older adults with sarcopenia may have difficulty maintaining balance while standing up, walking, turning, and sitting down. These limitations may increase the risk of falls and reduce independence in daily activities.

Elastic resistance training uses elastic bands to provide resistance during exercise. This type of exercise is relatively inexpensive, easy to perform, and allows the exercise load to be increased gradually according to each participant's ability. Adding elastic resistance training to routine physical exercise may improve lower-limb muscle function and dynamic balance more effectively than routine physical exercise alone.

This randomized controlled study will evaluate the effect of adding elastic resistance training to routine physical exercise on dynamic balance in older adults with sarcopenia living at Griya Wreda Jambangan, Surabaya. Participants will be assigned to either a group receiving routine physical exercise combined with elastic resistance training or a group receiving routine physical exercise alone. The intervention will be conducted for eight weeks. Dynamic balance will be assessed before and after the intervention using the Timed Up and Go test.

The investigators hypothesize that older adults who receive elastic resistance training in addition to routine physical exercise will demonstrate greater improvement in dynamic balance than those who receive routine physical exercise alone.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Timed Up and Go Test Completion Time at 8 Weeks
title: The Effect of Adding Elastic Resistance Training to Routine Exercise on Dynamic Balance in Older Adults With Sarcopenia at Griya Wreda Jambangan, Surabaya

brief_summary:
The goal of this multicenter observational study is to investigate the relationship between thyroid function, changes in thyroid hormone levels over time, and cardiovascular diseases in adults. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Are different thyroid function states and long-term changes in thyroid hormone levels associated with the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events? How do thyroid function abnormalities affect cardiac structure and function, and can these changes improve after thyroid function returns to normal? Researchers will compare participants with normal thyroid function, subclinical thyroid dysfunction, and overt thyroid dysfunction to evaluate differences in cardiovascular outcomes.The study includes retrospective and prospective cohorts. Researchers will collect thyroid function tests, clinical records, electrocardiograms, echocardiographic findings, treatment information, and long-term cardiovascular outcomes. Participants in the prospective cohort will undergo follow-up, with biological samples collected for exploratory analyses when appropriate and with informed consent. No experimental treatments will be assigned.
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital Xi'an Jiaotong University
primary_outcomes: Time to First Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event (MACE)
title: Thyroid Function and Cardiovascular Disease: The Thy-CVD Cohort

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare two surgical techniques for treating saddle nose deformity during rhinoplasty. It will also assess patient satisfaction and postoperative complications. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does a dorsal extended spreader graft with diced cartilage provide better aesthetic outcomes than a block graft with diced cartilage?
* Is there a difference in patient satisfaction between the two techniques?
* What complications occur after each surgical technique?

Participants will:

* Undergo rhinoplasty using either a dorsal extended spreader graft with diced cartilage or a block graft with diced cartilage.
* Attend postoperative follow-up visits at 1 week, 1 month, and 3 months.
* Have their nasal appearance and aesthetic outcome assessed by surgeons.
* Complete a patient satisfaction assessment using the Rhinoplasty Outcome Evaluation (ROE) score.
* Be assessed for complications such as infection, bruising, hematoma, warping, and dorsal irregularities.
interventions: Dorsal Extended Spreader Graft With Diced Cartilage
primary_outcomes: Aesthetic Outcome at 3 Months
Patient Satisfaction at 3 Months

brief_summary:
Stroke can cause weakness in one arm, making everyday activities such as eating, dressing, and personal care more difficult. Mirror therapy is a rehabilitation technique that uses the reflection of movements performed by the less-affected arm to create the visual impression that the affected arm is moving.

This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate whether adding lavender-based olfactory stimulation before mirror therapy improves upper extremity motor function and independence in activities of daily living compared with mirror therapy alone.

The study includes 22 individuals aged 65 years or older with post-stroke hemiparesis living in a long-term care institution. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups. The experimental group receives lavender-based olfactory stimulation followed by mirror therapy, while the control group receives mirror therapy alone.

Both groups undergo eight treatment sessions over two weeks. Upper extremity motor function and activities of daily living are assessed before and after the intervention using the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the Upper Extremity and the Barthel Index.

The study aims to determine whether adding olfactory stimulation to mirror therapy provides additional benefits for upper extremity rehabilitation after stroke.
primary_outcomes: Change in Upper Extremity Motor Function Assessed by the Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA-UE)
title: Mirror Therapy With Olfactory-Motor Priming for Arm Recovery After Stroke

brief_summary:
Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease that requires long-term monitoring. Although endoscopy is the gold standard for assessing intestinal inflammation, its invasive nature limits repeated use, particularly in children. Therefore, reliable noninvasive methods are needed to monitor disease activity.

This single-center, prospective observational study aims to evaluate the performance of the Mucosal Inflammation Noninvasive Index (MINI) and the Pediatric Crohn's Disease Activity Index (PCDAI) in children with Crohn's disease.

The study examines the relationship between MINI and PCDAI and evaluates their associations with endoscopic disease activity measured by the Simple Endoscopic Score for Crohn's Disease (SES-CD). It also compares the ability of both indices to identify patients with active intestinal inflammation.

The initial research hypothesis focused on evaluating the correlation between MINI and PCDAI. During the ongoing data collection period, the hypothesis was expanded to investigate whether MINI demonstrates superior discriminative performance compared with PCDAI in identifying endoscopic disease activity as assessed by SES-CD.
primary_outcomes: Correlation Between MINI and PCDAI in Pediatric Crohn's Disease
title: Comparative Study of Clinical Activity Indices of Crohn's Disease Patients Treated at Gazi University Pediatric Gastroenterology Clinic.

brief_summary:
The treatment of younger AML patients fit for intensive chemotherapy (IC) has long been based on a combination of an anthracycline and cytarabine as induction, followed by high-dose cytarabine (HDAC) consolidation, and possibly allogeneic stem-cell transplantation at least in non-favorable risk AML patients. Even if new agents like gemtuzumab ozogamicin (GO), FLT3 inhibitors, or CPX-351 have been approved to treat some patient subsets, there has been no major therapeutic advances to date in this field.

The first multicenter trial from the ALFA-FILO intergroup (Backbone InterGroup trial-1, BIG-1; NCT02416388; PHRC2010-03) randomly explored various standard intensive chemotherapy strategies, including higher-dose idarubicin vs. high-dose daunorubicin (DNR) and intermediate-dose cytarabine (IDAC) vs. HDAC in patients (18-60 years) with newly-diagnosed AML. This first part of the study, which enrolled 1405 participants between 01/2015 and 05/2019, showed that the benefit/risk ratio favored high-dose DNR for remission induction and IDAC consolidation, establishing the national standard treatment for younger AML patients. Six-year OS was 53.4% showing that there is still considerable room for improvement in this younger patient population.

High-throughput sequencing and multiparametric flow cytometry have significantly improved prognostic classifications and the evaluation of response to therapy through the quantification of measurable residual disease (MRD). Many studies have shown that the higher the MRD, the higher the risk of relapse and death; and recent guidelines have included MRD in the response criteria. Achieving complete remission without MRD is a major goal after first-line treatment to guide subsequent treatments, including transplantation. Furthermore, MRD follow-up in patients who achieved complete remission is becoming a major issue, as patients treated for molecular relapse appear to have a better prognosis than patients treated for morphological relapse. Preliminary data also showed encouraging results from salvage treatment at the time of MRD relapse.

Quizartinib (a second-generation FLT3-ITD inhibitor) and venetoclax (the first-in-class BCL-2 inhibitor) have been recently approved for the treatment of AML. Quizartinib was approved on the basis of a placebo-controlled trial but its added value compared to midostaurin (first FLT3 inhibitor available in this indication since 2018) has never been prospectively explored. Although venetoclax was approved for first line therapy of patients who are unfit for intensive chemotherapy, it is widely used in relapsed or refractory younger patients. Venetoclax combined with intensive salvage chemotherapy is feasible and induce a high rate of CR. However, no prospective, randomized trial demonstrated venetoclax efficacy in this setting.
primary_outcomes: Sub-Study 1 : MRD response
Sub-Study 2 : MRD response venetoclax
Sub-Study 3 : Overall survival
title: Prospective Evaluation of Response to Treatment in Younger Adult Patients (18-60 Years) With Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether brief self-improvement exercises, practiced daily on a smartphone for four weeks, reduce depression, anxiety, and stress in adults in the United States, and which exercises help most. Participants are adults who are interested in self-improvement and have not had severe mental health challenges in the past two months. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does daily practice of brief self-improvement exercises lower depression, anxiety, and stress compared with daily mood tracking alone?
* Which of 21 different exercises lower depression, anxiety, and stress compared with daily mood tracking alone?

Researchers will compare participants who practice the exercises with participants who only track their mood each day to see if the exercises reduce depression, anxiety, and stress. Researchers will also compare the exercises with each other, including a few minutes of quiet rest, to learn which ones help most, which ones improve mood right away, and which ones people keep doing.

Participants will:

* Complete an online survey at the start of the study and again after four weeks
* Use the free Thought Saver smartphone app every day for 28 days
* Answer 4 short questions about their mood, energy, and productivity each day (about 1 minute)
* If assigned to the exercise group, also do 3 short exercises each day (about 2 to 3 minutes each), drawn from a personal set of 5 exercises such as gratitude writing, breathing exercises, meditation, or planning a small step toward a goal
interventions: Reflective Writing About a Happy Experience
Connect with Someone You Care About
primary_outcomes: Depression as assessed by Patient Health Questionnaire-8 (PHQ-8)
Anxiety as assessed by Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) questionnaire
Stress as assessed by Perceived Stress Scale 10-item version (PSS-10)
title: Comparing Brief, Low-Intensity Self-Improvement Exercises in a Non-Clinical Population

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured, multi-component intervention package-the TIPS system-in improving the workflow and outcomes of endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke caused by large vessel occlusion (LVO) in China. Despite EVT being a guideline-recommended therapy, delays in workflow processes such as door-to-puncture time (DTP) and puncture-to-reperfusion time (PRT) remain widespread, especially in developing countries. The TIPS intervention focuses on key structure-process-outcome (SPO) elements and includes training \& discussion, indicator feedback, professional guidance, and a solutions toolkit, implemented through a PDSA (Plan-Do-Study-Act) cycle. This multicenter, cluster-randomized study will assess whether the TIPS intervention improves EVT process efficiency and patient functional outcomes (90-day mRS). The findings are expected to support quality improvement and promote equitable stroke care delivery across China.
primary_outcomes: Door-to-Puncture Time (DTP)
title: Improving Endovascular Treatment Through Process Refinements
