brief_summary:
Dialysis is important in treating people with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) to remove excess water and toxins, maintaining quality of life (QoL) and to keep people alive. Where people with ESKD retain too much water (fluid overload), the amount of water removed and the speed of removal must be higher to meet the individual's needs and avoid short- and long-term negative consequences. This can be a particular issue for people on haemodialysis after a weekend, when there is a 2-day gap between dialysis sessions. Removing the larger quantities of water quickly (proportional to speed of removal) can lead to low blood pressure, reducing QoL and increasing the chance of getting heart and blood vessel disease and the risk of death. Additionally, the dialysis schedules, and lack of dialysis capacity, often means sessions cannot be extended, or patients are offered extra sessions for fluid removal. Given the need to reduce fluid overload and the difficulties people have sticking to fluid restrictions, (taken by mouth) other therapies are needed to improve outcomes and people's experiences.

One such possible therapy is to induce sweating via passive heating (i.e. sitting in hot tubs). Few studies have examined sweat loss rates with heating in people with ESKD. Given the potential cost-effective method for reducing excessive body water and improving QoL, there is little evidence with no data examining any associated cardiovascular or quality of life benefits.
primary_outcomes: Interdialytic Weight Gain (IDWG):
Deviation from Dry Weight:
title: Hot Water Immersion on Fluid Overload in People With End-stage Kidney Disease

brief_summary:
Approximately 275'000 people in Switzerland harbor an unruptured intracranial aneurysm (UIA). Rupture leads to subarachnoid hemorrhage, which is associated with high morbidity and mortality and causes 25% of all cerebrovascular-related deaths. UIAs cause a relevant healthcare burden, which is increasing due to the extensive use of neuroimaging. They pose a challenge to both patients and physicians: Patients have to live with the diagnosis of an aneurysm that can cause a rupture with severe consequences. Physicians have to judge whether the risks of preventive occlusion are lower than those of natural history. Management consists of observation with follow-up imaging or preventive aneurysm occlusion weighing up the risk of natural history against the risk of treatment. Estimating rupture risks of UIAs in an individual patient is the crucial step in clinical decision-making.

Older studies suggested that small UIA (\<7mm) have a negligible rupture risk and most incidental UIAs are small. Following this logic, most patients with UIA do not require preventive treatment. However, 70-80% of patients presenting with subarachnoid hemorrhage carry aneurysms \<7 mm in size, leading to the so-called "aneurysm-rupture paradox". Newer evidence shows that UIAs have a heterogenous natural history: They can either form and remain stable for a long time or present an unstable course, entertained by wall inflammation, leading to aneurysm growth, and ultimately rupture.

The main clinical challenge in UIA is to correctly identify aneurysms that have an unstable course out of the increasing amount of incidentally detected UIAs and offer preventive treatment to these selected patients. Growth during follow-up, irregular aneurysm shape, hypertension, and smoking are currently used as main surrogate parameters to predict an unstable UIA.

Ultra-high field 7 Tesla MRI (UHF 7T MRI) has become clinically available as a new imaging modality. Due to the higher field strength, UHF 7T MRI enables imaging with an increased signal-to-noise ratio resulting in significantly improved vessel wall imaging and spatial resolution to detect AWE and morphological changes with high precision. With these properties, UHF 7T MRI has the potential to overcome current limitations of vessel wall imaging in 3T MRI by providing information on AWE with increased specificity omitting the high false positive rates that make AWE as a biomarker in 3T MRI not useful.

After obtaining the signed informed consent and inclusion in the study, demographics will be assessed. The 3T MRI and 7T UHF MRI follow-up examination will be scheduled as a next step, and the appointment will be communicated to the participant. The timing of the 3T + 7T UHF MRI examination is not determined by the date of enrolment but by the timing of the baseline examination and must be no later than 12±1 months after that.

The exam will take place at the Translational Imaging center in Sitem-insel. Before the MRI examination, participants are asked to provide information on risk factors for UIA and medication history via a questionnaire. For the MRI examination, a 3 T scanner will be used with a standard head coil provided by the the MR-vendor and a 7 T whole-body MRI scanner equipped with a 1-channel transmit and 32-channel receive head coil. The 7T protocoll will comprose arterial ToF angiography and vessel wall imaging sequences (T1 SPACE and T1 SE dark blood). The acquisition time is approximately 44 minutes. The 3T examination will be performed according to the clinical standard protocol. After the examination, participants can go directly home and no further examinations will be performed at this appointment.

According to the standard of care at our institutions, all follow-up examinations of patients with UIA, who have been assigned to observation with MRI, will be discussed at the interdisciplinary aneurysm board. Within 4-8 weeks after the 3T + 7T UHF MRI examination, a chart review of the board decision and outpatient visits will be performed to determine whether management changed from observation to intervention. Furthermore, the occurrence of subarachnoid hemorrhage during the study period will be recorded if applicable.
lead_sponsor: Insel Gruppe AG, University Hospital Bern

title: Follow-up of Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms With Ultra-High Field 7 Tesla MRI

brief_summary:
The management of atherosclerotic carotid disease, according to current guidelines, is primarily based on the quantification of the degree of carotid stenosis, together with the assessment of its hemodynamic significance and the presence of neurological symptoms, such as transient ischemic attack (TIA) or stroke. However, these parameters may not fully reflect the hemodynamic impact of carotid lesions on peripheral vascular territories, particularly the ocular circulation.

The eye represents the only vascular territory that can be directly visualized in vivo, providing a unique "window" into the microcirculation. Retinal and choroidal abnormalities resulting from chronic hypoperfusion may reflect the degree of hemodynamic impairment associated with carotid disease and provide additional information beyond the anatomical characteristics of the stenosis identified by vascular imaging alone.

From a vascular surgery perspective, ophthalmological assessment and fundus examination could allow a more accurate phenotypic characterization of patients with carotid disease, identifying individuals in whom carotid stenosis has already resulted in end-organ microvascular consequences despite the absence of major neurological manifestations. In the era of personalized medicine, such a multidisciplinary approach could move beyond a purely morphological assessment of carotid plaque by incorporating functional and clinical parameters that may potentially contribute to therapeutic decision-making.

The results of the present study may therefore help define the role of fundus examination, combined with a more comprehensive assessment of ocular symptoms, as a complementary tool in the evaluation of patients with carotid stenosis. This approach may facilitate a more accurate identification of patients at higher risk of disease progression and cerebrovascular ischemic events, while potentially improving the selection of candidates for carotid revascularization procedures
primary_outcomes: Correlation between carotid stenosis and ocular symptoms
title: Evalutation of Ocular Symptoms in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial compared two timings of the same prophylactic carbetocin dose in grand multiparous women (five or more previous deliveries) undergoing vaginal delivery. Women received 100 µg intravenous carbetocin either immediately after delivery of the anterior shoulder (before placental delivery) or immediately after complete placental expulsion (after placental delivery). The main question was whether earlier administration reduces postpartum hemorrhage, and whether it affects placental delivery, including the need for manual removal of the placenta.
lead_sponsor: Dr. Lutfi Kirdar Kartal Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Postpartum Hemorrhage
title: Timing of Carbetocin Administration in Grand Multiparous Women

brief_summary: The goal of this explored study intends to investigate how different types of speed, agility, and quickness (SAQ) exercises effect the body's immediate hormonal and physiological reactions in young male volleyball players. Physical exercise can alter the release of hormones and other substances involved in the body's response to physical effort and stress. However, it is still ambiguous if activities that necessitate swift reflexes to unforeseen visual stimuli provide distinct outcomes in contrast to conventional exercises that entail premeditated movements. The study will include 36 competitive male volleyball players under 19 years of age from the Algerian Amateur League. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups, with 12 players in each group. The first group will conduct a 10-minute reactive training session using BlazePod, an interactive lighting system that requires participants to respond swiftly to visual inputs. The second cohort will engage in a 20-minute session with the identical approach, featuring increased workout repetitions and varied rest intervals. The third group will do 10 minutes of standard volleyball-related workouts without interactive visual indications. All participants will complete one supervised workout session. Blood samples will be collected roughly five minutes before exercise and within two minutes after exercise to assess five substances: epinephrine (adrenaline), norepinephrine (noradrenaline), dopamine, cortisol, and cortisone. These chemicals are involved in the body's responses to physical exertion and stress. Heart rate will also be recorded, and participants will report how physically challenging they found the exercises using a simple grading scale. Investigators will analyse data collected prior to and following physical activity and assess if the variations differ among the three cohorts. The study intends to better understanding of how exercise duration, physical demands, and responsiveness to visual signals may influence acute hormonal responses in young volleyball players. The results could assist researchers and sports experts in comprehending the physical requirements of reactionary exercise and inform subsequent studies on athletic training. The study is not meant to assess if these activities increase long-term sports performance. No results are currently available, and it is not yet known whether one workout strategy will create distinct hormonal reactions from another.
conditions: Acute Catecholamine and Glucocorticoid Responses to Physical Performance
primary_outcomes: Change in Plasma Epinephrine Level
Change in Plasma Norepinephrine Level
Change in Plasma Dopamine Level
Change in Serum Cortisol Level
Change in Serum Cortisone Level
title: Neuroendocrine Responses to High-Intensity Reactive Exercises: Effects on Catecholamine and Hormonal Profiles in Elite U-19 Volleyball Players

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether burnout is related to the intention to migrate abroad among physiotherapists working in Türkiye, and whether job satisfaction explains this relationship. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do effort-reward imbalance and exposure to workplace violence increase burnout?
* Does burnout reduce job satisfaction, and does lower job satisfaction increase the intention to migrate abroad?
* Does foreign language proficiency strengthen the relationship between burnout and migration intention?

Participants will complete a single anonymous online survey of about 20 minutes, including sociodemographic questions, the Burnout Assessment Tool (BAT-TR), the Effort-Reward Imbalance Questionnaire, the Job Satisfaction Scale, and the Brain Drain Attitude Scale.
primary_outcomes: Intention to Migrate Abroad (Brain Drain Attitude Scale Score)
title: Burnout and Migration Intention Among Physiotherapists in Türkiye

brief_summary:
This study will compare changes in the function of the right side of the heart after successful treatment of a long-standing complete blockage in either the right coronary artery or the left circumflex coronary artery. Patients will receive catheter-based treatment because their clinical team has independently decided that it is appropriate; the study will not assign their artery or treatment technique.

The planned comparison includes 160 patients with successful treatment, with 80 in each artery group. Heart ultrasound will be performed within 14 days before the procedure and again six months afterward. A telephone follow-up will take place at three months. Conventional ultrasound measurements and speckle tracking, which measures deformation of the heart muscle, will be used to assess right ventricular function. The main comparison is the change in right ventricular free-wall longitudinal strain between the two groups.
interventions: Resting conventional and RV speckle tracking echocardiography
primary_outcomes: Change in right ventricular free-wall longitudinal strain magnitude
title: Right Ventricular Function After Successful Reopening of Right Coronary Versus Left Circumflex Chronic Total Occlusions

brief_summary:
This is a single-arm, prospective exploratory clinical study. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of trastuzumab rezetecan (SHR-A1811) combined with toripalimab and endocrine therapy as neoadjuvant treatment for patients with stage II-III HR-positive, HER2-low primary breast cancer.

Eligible participants will receive the combination neoadjuvant regimen before surgery. The primary endpoint is pathological complete response (pCR, ypT0/is ypN0) rate after surgery. Secondary endpoints include objective response rate (ORR), residual cancer burden (RCB), event-free survival (EFS), overall survival (OS), and safety.

A total of 30 participants will be enrolled. The recruitment period will last for 12 months. All enrolled subjects will receive study treatment and follow-up according to the study protocol.
lead_sponsor: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital
primary_outcomes: Pathological Complete Response Rate (pCR, ypT0/isN0)
title: Neoadjuvant Trastuzumab Rezetecan Plus Toripalimab and Endocrine Therapy in HR-Positive HER2-Low Breast Cancer

brief_summary: This study is a randomized, single-blind, sham-controlled trial to assess the efficacy and safety of a series of two sets (four total) of bilateral Study Procedures (SGB or Sham) administered to adults with Long COVID (Figure 1) followed by a sham-to-active OLE trial. Approximately 272 (136 per arm) participants will be randomized 1:1 to receive SGB or a sham Study Procedure. Following screening and completion of baseline PROs, eligible participants will undergo in-person baseline assessments and blood draw. Those who are confirmed to be eligible will complete a pre-procedure telehealth visit and then be randomized 1:1 at Day 1 to receive either active SGB (Arm 1) or sham (Arm 2); each administration is referred to as a "Study Procedure". Participants will receive a total of four Study Procedures with follow up visits to assess recovery. Outcomes will be assessed at 28 days, 56 days, 12 weeks, and 26 weeks. Follow-up visits at weeks 12 and 26 allow for assessment of durability of response and delayed adverse events (AEs). The primary objective is to compare the change in overall HRQoL from baseline to 8 weeks between participants aged 18-65 years with Long COVID randomized to a series of two sets of bilateral SGB or sham Study Procedures.
lead_sponsor: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
primary_outcomes: Change in the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) 29+2 Preference (PROPr) score

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial will evaluate the effect of a low glycemic index (GI) diet on symptoms of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and adolescents. A total of 128 participants aged 6 to ≤18 years, diagnosed with ADHD according to the Conners Parent Rating Scale-48 (CPRS-48), will be recruited from the pediatric neurology outpatient clinic at Kafrelsheikh University Hospital and randomly assigned in equal numbers (64 per group) to one of two arms. The intervention group will receive a structured low-GI diet (whole grains, legumes, low-GI non-starchy vegetables and fruits, and lean proteins, with refined flour, white rice, and sugary snacks limited) delivered through the Clinical Nutrition Unit, supported by a low-GI pyramid teaching tool, regular dietary counseling, and weekly dietitian review of 3-day food records to monitor adherence. The control group will continue a normal diet. ADHD symptoms will be assessed with the Conners 48 scale at baseline, 1 month, and 6 months. Children with other neurological conditions, autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability, severe psychiatric conditions, chronic illnesses, diabetes, celiac disease, or food allergies requiring dietary restrictions will be excluded. Written informed consent will be obtained from parents or guardians, and the study has ethics committee approval (REC-KFSIRB200, Kafrelsheikh University).

brief_summary: Incontinence after prostate treatment (IPT) affects up to 25% of men following radical prostatectomy or other prostate therapies, primarily resulting from sphincteric weakness and impaired neuromuscular control. Current management options, including behavioral therapy and surgical implants, are often limited by modest effectiveness or invasiveness. Emerging neuroimaging evidence demonstrates that the pelvic supplementary motor area (pSMA) in the brain plays a critical regulatory role in controlling pelvic floor muscles and urethral sphincter activity. This proof-of-concept, prospective, randomized clinical trial aims to evaluate the safety, tolerability, acceptability, and procedural feasibility of targeting the pSMA using non-invasive repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in adult males with IPT, alongside a cohort of continent controls. A total of 23 participants will be enrolled (targeting 10 evaluable IPT subjects and 10 continent controls). Participants undergo baseline fMRI using a natural bladder filling protocol, and a randomized, single-session neuronavigated rTMS protocol with concurrent pelvic floor electromyography (EMG) and functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) to evaluate physiological and neurofunctional changes. Safety and adverse events are monitored closely through a 1-month virtual follow-up visit. Findings from this study will establish foundational evidence for cortical modulation of pelvic floor control in IPT. Additionally, these results will guide the design of a future larger, clinical trial to optimize rTMS parameters and integrate brain neuromodulation into post-prostate treatment rehabilitation strategies.
primary_outcomes: Recruitment and Retention Rate
Acceptability of Intervention
Adverse Events
title: rTMS for Incontinence After Prostate Treatment

brief_summary:
Vitamin D is important for bone health and other functions of the body. In Slovenia, vitamin D levels are often low during the autumn and winter months because sunlight exposure is insufficient for the body to produce enough vitamin D.

The purpose of this study was to assess vitamin D levels in adults in Slovenia and compare the effects of two daily doses of vitamin D3 (2,000 IU and 4,000 IU) with a placebo (a spray containing no active vitamin D).

This was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups: 2,000 IU of vitamin D3 per day, 4,000 IU of vitamin D3 per day, or placebo. All products were administered as oral sprays for 12 weeks. Neither the participants nor the researchers performing the measurements knew which treatment each participant received.

Blood samples were collected at the beginning and end of the study to measure serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D \[25(OH)D\] concentrations. Height and body weight were also measured to calculate body mass index (BMI).

The main aim was to determine how much serum vitamin D levels changed after 12 weeks in each group. The researchers also examined whether the response to supplementation differed according to BMI, age, and sex.

The findings may help improve understanding of vitamin D supplementation needs in adults, particularly during the winter months.
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum 25-Hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] Concentration From Baseline to 12 Weeks
title: Effects of Different Doses of Vitamin D3 Supplementation on Serum Vitamin D Levels in Adults

brief_summary: The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effect of animation video-assisted fall prevention education on fall prevention behaviors in older patients with cancer receiving outpatient chemotherapy. Participants were randomly assigned to either an intervention group, which received animation video-assisted fall prevention training in addition to standard institutional care, or a control group, which received routine standard care alone. Fall prevention behaviors were assessed at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months post-intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Fall Behavior Scores
title: Animated Video Training for Fall Prevention in Older Cancer Patients

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to find out whether hearing tests performed with the Oscilla A60 audiometer, where the patient largely tests themselves with minimal staff assistance, are accurate enough to be used for diagnosing hearing loss and as the sole basis for fitting hearing aids. Adults referred for their first hearing aids at Aalborg University Hospital will have their hearing tested both with the Oscilla audiometer and by a trained audiology assistant at the same visit. Participants are then randomly assigned to receive hearing aids fitted based on either the Oscilla hearing test or the audiology assistant's hearing test. The main questions are: (1) Do the Oscilla results agree with the audiology assistant's results for both air-conduction and bone-conduction hearing thresholds? (2) Do participants fitted based on the Oscilla test report a hearing benefit that is not worse than that of participants fitted based on the standard test, two months after fitting?

brief_summary:
This pilot study will examine whether taking urolithin A helps healthcare workers stay focused after a night shift. It will also look at changes in fatigue, sleepiness, sleep patterns, and the body's internal clock.

The study plans to enroll 40 physicians and nurses aged 24 to 55 who work scheduled night shifts at Henan Provincial People's Hospital. Participants will be assigned by chance, in equal numbers, to take either 1 gram of urolithin A or a matching placebo capsule by mouth once each morning for five consecutive days, starting the day before the night shift. Participants and the study staff who give out the capsules or assess outcomes will not know which group each participant is in. Participants will follow their usual work schedules.

The main measure is the Stroop interference effect, which is the difference in average response time between correct answers when a color word conflicts with its displayed color and correct answers when they match. The researchers will compare how this measure changes from two days before the night shift to the scheduled follow-up assessments in the two groups.

Participants will also rate their fatigue and sleepiness, wear a wrist device to track sleep, keep a sleep diary, and provide saliva samples to measure melatonin. They will complete tasks that measure alertness and the ability to withhold a response during three MRI scans scheduled before the night shift, on the morning the shift ends, and during recovery. The study will help estimate how much the main measure varies among participants to inform a larger trial.
conditions: Attention, Sleep, and Circadian Rhythms After Night Shifts in Healthcare Workers
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in the Stroop Reaction Time Interference Effect
title: Urolithin A and Its Effects on Attention and Sleep Timing in Healthcare Workers After Night Shifts

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether therapy in a multisensory room improves sensory processing, behavioural and attentional regulation and stress in children aged 3 to 12 years with autism spectrum disorder (support level 2-3), and whether it reduces stress in their main caregivers. The main question it aims to answer is: does sensory processing (Sensory Profile 2) change more after 8 weeks of multisensory room therapy than after 8 weeks of standard behavioural therapy? Researchers will also compare executive function, attention and behaviour, parental stress, and stress-related biomarkers in saliva (cortisol, oxytocin and inflammatory interleukins). They will also record physiological stress signals in caregivers (heart rate, skin conductance, breathing and temperature).

Sixty children will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Children in the first group will receive two individual 45-minute multisensory room sessions per week for 8 weeks. Children in the second group will receive standard behavioural therapy with psychology and speech therapy, without multisensory stimulation. Caregivers will complete questionnaires and give saliva samples before and after the 8-week programme.
primary_outcomes: Change in sensory hyper-reactivity (Sensory Profile 2, Sensitivity quadrant)
title: Multisensory Room Therapy for Stress and Sensory Regulation in Children With Autism and Their Caregivers

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a modified way of preparing the tooth surface improves the results of resin infiltration in adults with white spot lesions (chalky white marks caused by loss of minerals from the tooth enamel) who want to improve the appearance of their teeth.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Does preparing the tooth surface with a modified microabrasion technique (6.6% hydrochloric acid combined with silicon carbide particles) make white spot lesions blend better with the natural tooth color than the conventional method (15% hydrochloric acid etching), immediately after treatment, after 1 week, and after 1 month?

Researchers will compare the two surface preparation methods to see which one gives a better color match with the surrounding healthy enamel.

Participants will:

* Have their white spot lesions examined and graded using a fluorescence camera, photographed, and scanned with an intraoral scanner.
* Be assigned by chance to one of the two surface preparation methods, followed by resin infiltration in a single visit.
* Return after 1 week and 1 month for follow-up photographs to measure tooth color.
interventions: Conventional 15% HCl etching and resin infiltration
lead_sponsor: University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City
primary_outcomes: Change in Lesion Color (ΔE) From Baseline to Immediately After Treatment

brief_summary:
Migraine is a common disabling primary headache disorder ranked as the third most prevalent disorder in the world. Chronic migraine (CM) is described as a headache occurring on 15 or more days/month for more than 3 months, which, on at least 8 days/month, has the features of a migraine headache. Chronic migraine typically evolves from episodic migraine with an annual progression rate of \~3%. CM is an important treatable cause of neurological disability . It impacts, on an average, 1.4-2.2% of the global population and imposes a significant individual and socioeconomic burden with disability scores reported to be nearly twice as high.

It is vital to make a diagnosis and ensure that any concomitant medical or psychological conditions are treated in parallel with interventions aimed at reducing the biological tendency to headaches. The conventional treatment for migraine therapy is medical therapy. However only half of the patients respond to medications and preventive drug treatments; and about 10% discontinue medications due to adverse events. Moreover almost half of the patients are not satisfied with the present treatment. There is a clear need for additional preventive strategies in the current treatment regimens for migraines due to existing shortcomings of medical management of CM. In addition, there are other tactics that can be used, such as practicing alternative medicine through Yoga and Meditation.

Meditation has been found to help in reducing stress and changing the psychological state of a person. Mindfulness meditation has been derived from Vipassana, an age old meditation technique and has been practiced since long. Buddhist literature has detailed description about the techniques of Vipassana. Mindfulness of Breathing called as 'Anapanasati Meditation', in Buddhist scriptures is the first step in the practice of Vipassana meditation. It is a technique that involves observing natural and normal breathing. As it enters and exits the body our breath acts as a connection between our conscious and unconscious minds and the voluntary and involuntary processes of our body. By observing our breath, we can gain insight into the nature of our mind and its tendency to be inconsistent and fleeting.Slowly, this technique helps develop concentration of the mind and become calm. . It is a simple and scientific method that can be easily learned. Using Mindfulness of Breathing (Anapanasati) as a tool to reduce stress can be helpful in reducing the disability associated with migraines, as stress is a common trigger for migraines.

In the present study we aim to evaluate the beneficial effects of this simple meditation technique in management of CM.
primary_outcomes: To assess the change in headache days at 12 weeks from baseline.
title: The Effect of 'Mindfulness of Breathing' on Chronic Migraine

brief_summary:
This study examines whether a psychoeducation program based on spiritual reminiscence therapy improves spiritual well-being and reduces depressive symptoms in adults aged 65 years and older living in nursing homes in Türkiye. Spiritual reminiscence involves reflecting on past experiences, personal values, beliefs, and relationships that give life meaning.

The intervention consists of 12 small-group sessions delivered twice a week over six weeks. Each session lasts approximately 40-50 minutes and is led by the researcher. Participants discuss meaningful life experiences, relationships, losses, worries, sources of strength, personal beliefs, and hopes for the future. Activities include sharing memories and meaningful objects, reflecting on past ways of coping with difficulties, and identifying achievable goals. Participants in the control group continue to receive the nursing home's usual care.

Spiritual well-being and depressive symptoms are assessed before the program, immediately after the program, and one month after its completion. The study compares the intervention and control groups to determine whether the program improves spiritual well-being and reduces depressive symptoms, and whether any benefits remain at the one-month follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Spiritual Well-Being at the End of the Intervention Assessed With the FACIT-Sp-12

Both groups completed questionnaires before the intervention and approximately one month later. The questionnaires assessed attitudes toward caring for dying patients, attitudes toward supporting patients' families, and confidence in providing palliative care.

brief_summary:
This study evaluates how accurately a simple ultrasound test, the sliding sign, predicts intra-abdominal adhesions before a repeat cesarean delivery. Adhesions are bands of scar tissue that can form between the uterus, the bladder and the abdominal wall after a cesarean delivery. Adhesions can lengthen the next operation, delay delivery of the baby, increase bleeding and raise the risk of injury to the bladder or bowel.

The sliding sign is checked by placing a standard ultrasound probe on the abdomen while the woman breathes deeply. Free sliding of the uterus under the abdominal wall suggests that adhesions are unlikely; absence of sliding suggests that adhesions are present. The test takes 2 to 3 minutes, is painless, has no known risk to the mother or the baby, and adds no cost.

Pregnant women with at least one previous cesarean delivery who are scheduled for a planned repeat cesarean delivery at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital are invited to take part. The sliding sign is checked within 2 hours before surgery. During the operation, a surgeon who does not know the ultrasound result grades any adhesions on a standard four-grade scale, and the ultrasound result is compared with these surgical findings. The study also compares operative times, blood loss and complications between women with and without free sliding of the uterus, and examines whether the test performs differently after one previous cesarean delivery than after two or more. Taking part does not change the planned surgery or any other aspect of care.
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity of the Sliding Sign for Significant Intra-Abdominal Adhesions
Specificity of the Sliding Sign for Significant Intra-Abdominal Adhesions (Grade 2-3)
title: Ultrasound Sliding Sign for Predicting Abdominal Adhesions Before Repeat Cesarean Delivery

brief_summary:
\### Brief Summary

Femoral fractures can cause severe pain during and after surgery. Although fascia iliaca block is commonly used to relieve pain in patients undergoing femoral fracture surgery, the duration of pain relief may be limited.

Dexmedetomidine is a medication that may prolong the pain-relieving effect of local anesthetics such as bupivacaine. However, the most appropriate dose of dexmedetomidine for this type of nerve block is not yet clearly established.

This study aims to determine the lowest effective dose of dexmedetomidine when added to bupivacaine for ultrasound-guided fascia iliaca block in patients undergoing femoral fracture surgery under general anesthesia.

The study includes 90 adult patients, aged 18-75 years, who are scheduled for femoral fracture surgery. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups, with 30 patients in each group. All patients will receive general anesthesia and an ultrasound-guided fascia iliaca block containing 30 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine, combined with one of the following doses of dexmedetomidine:

* Group A: 0.5 micrograms/kg.
* Group B: 0.75 micrograms/kg.
* Group C: 1 microgram/kg.

Neither the patients nor the doctors assessing the study outcomes will know which dose has been administered.

Pain levels will be assessed during the first 24 hours after surgery using a numerical pain scale. The study will also measure the time until patients first require additional pain medication and the total amount of pain medication used.

Other assessments will include leg muscle strength, level of sedation, heart rate, blood pressure, and any possible side effects or complications.

The main purpose of this study is to identify the lowest dose of dexmedetomidine that provides effective postoperative pain relief while minimizing unwanted effects, helping improve pain management and recovery after femoral fracture surgery.
primary_outcomes: Time to the first request for rescue analgesia in minutes
title: Dexmedetomidine as an Adjuvant to Bupivacaine in Fascia Iliaca Block for Femoral Fracture Surgery Under General Anesthesia: A Dose-Finding Study

brief_summary:

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is this technique feasible approach to assess food intolerances in patients with IBD and IBS?
* Does patients with IBD and IBS exhibit acute tissue changes upon exposure to specific food antigens?

Researches will compare the food antigen to a placebo solution (saline solution without an antigen) to see if the reaction in the tissue is different.

Participants will:

* Answer questionnaires.
* Provide a blood and stool sample.
* Take an allergy test.
* Undergo an upper endoscopy.

brief_summary:
To investigate potential major intraoperative and postoperative complications associated with the use of the DaVinci SP® robotic system-via either an intercostal or subcostal approach-during anatomical lung resections in thoracic surgery.

Major complications include: intraoperative conversion to a different surgical technique (thoracoscopy, multi-port robotic surgery) or a different access method (thoracotomy, placement of additional trocars); the need for unplanned intraoperative maneuvers not included in the standard surgical procedure; and the development of bronchopleural fistulas within 10 days.

A single-center, randomized, two-arm (1:1) pilot experimental study on a surgical procedure, investigating the use of two different approaches with the Da Vinci SP® robotic system for anatomical lung resections in thoracic surgery.
primary_outcomes: Total percentage of major complications
title: INSPiRE - INtercostal Single Port Robot Evaluation

brief_summary:
Extracranial malignant germ cell tumors (GCTs) account for about 3% of childhood cancers. The current international risk classification (Malignant Germ Cell International Consortium, MaGIC) is based on age, primary tumor site and stage, and does not include how tumor markers respond during treatment. Serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is measured routinely in nearly all of these children.

This national, multicenter, retrospective cohort study will evaluate whether the rate of AFP decline during first-line treatment predicts event-free survival independently of MaGIC risk factors. The medical records of children younger than 18 years diagnosed with an extracranial malignant non-germinomatous GCT between January 2014 and December 2025 and treated at participating pediatric oncology centers in Turkey will be reviewed. No new tests, samples, visits or interventions are required.

Secondary aims are to evaluate the prognostic value of AFP at diagnosis and of beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG) decline kinetics, to describe postoperative AFP kinetics in patients managed with surgery alone, to describe how relapses are detected, to quantify long-term treatment-related toxicity according to treatment intensity, and to explore a subgroup of patients who might be candidates for treatment reduction in future prospective studies.
primary_outcomes: Event-free survival according to alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) decline kinetics
title: Alpha-Fetoprotein Decline Kinetics in Children With Extracranial Malignant Germ Cell Tumors

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to investigate the relationship between liver health and cardiovascular diseases in adults. The study aims to understand how liver fat, liver scarring, and other liver changes are related to heart structure, heart function, and cardiovascular events over time.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Are liver imaging features and liver-related blood test results associated with the risk of developing cardiovascular diseases?
* Are changes in liver health associated with changes in heart structure and function?
* Are liver-related changes associated with major cardiovascular events, including heart attack, stroke, heart failure hospitalization, and cardiovascular death?

Researchers will study two groups of participants: a retrospective cohort, using existing medical records and imaging data, and a prospective cohort, following participants over time.

Participants in the prospective cohort will have their medical information, laboratory results, and imaging findings collected during routine care. They will also provide blood and other biological samples, with informed consent, for future research. Researchers will follow participants to assess changes in liver health, heart function, and cardiovascular outcomes. No study treatment will be assigned, and participants will continue to receive their usual medical care.
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital Xi'an Jiaotong University
primary_outcomes: Time to First Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event (MACE)
title: Cardiohepatic Cohort: The Heart-Liver Axis Study

brief_summary:
This study will examine whether combining sirolimus (also called rapamycin) with intravenous esketamine may reduce depression symptoms in adults whose depression did not improve sufficiently after a previous course of intravenous esketamine. Researchers will also assess side effects and how long any improvement lasts.

Approximately 40 adults aged 18 to 60 years will participate at two centers in Sao Paulo State, Brazil. All participants will receive the same treatment: eight esketamine infusions over 4 weeks and a dose of oral sirolimus before the first infusion of each week. There is no placebo group.

After providing informed consent, potential participants will undergo interviews, questionnaires, medical assessments, laboratory testing, and review of records from their previous treatment. Eligible participants will complete symptom questionnaires and clinical ratings before and during treatment and at follow-up visits through Week 12. Dissociation and sedation will be assessed before each infusion and at 40 and 120 minutes after the infusion starts. Additional depression ratings will be obtained 24 hours after the first and last infusions. Clinical monitoring and discharge decisions will be managed by the treating hospital team.

The main outcome is the change in clinician-rated depression severity from the assessment before the first study dose to Week 5, which is 7 days after the last esketamine infusion.
primary_outcomes: Mean Change From Baseline in Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) Total Score at Week 5
title: Esketamine Plus Sirolimus for Adults With Depression Who Have Not Responded to Esketamine

brief_summary:
This study aims to assess the effectiveness of Intensive Case Management (ICM) compared to TAU. Economically, this study could contribute to more cost-effective treatments, since relatively expensive inpatient care could be relieved of patients not benefiting from inpatient care, and those patients would receive a more adequate and effective treatment. Our first goal is to evaluate the effectivenessof ICM as a treatment for people with SUDs in the canton of Aargau compared to TAU. To assess the effectiveness, the outcome measured will be the RICID and the NOIA. Furthermore, the increase in Quality of Life and Social Integration with appropriate Questionnaires of Patients in ICM is compared to Patients in TAU. The second goal of this study is to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of ICM for the aforementioned patients compared to TAU.

Case Management, especially for people with multiple and complex needs, is an intervention designed to enhance coordination and continuity of support and care (Vanderplasschen et al. 2019). Also, for people with high levels of disability due to mental illness, ICM is widely claimed to be an evidence-based and cost-effective program (King, 2006). Furthermore, key ICM components, linkage and retention, seem to show the largest effect sizes (SMD = 0.33, 95% CI 0.18-0.48) in ICM. Linkage and retention are necessary prerequisites that keep patients with SUDs in contact with health services (Vanderplasschen et al., 2019). Although evidence across all outcome measures, according to the same author, is significant and positive, but small (SMD = 0.18, 95% CI \[0.07-0.28\]). There is mixed evidence in outcomes such as health outcomes (SMD = -0.16, 95%CI \[-0.40, 0.08\]), social functioning (SMD = 0.14, 95% CI \[-0.01, 0.28\]) or reduced substance use (SMD = 0.10, 95% CI \[-0.02, 0.21\]).

Moreover, ICM and closely related models (i.e., Assertive Community Treatment, ACT) show a Reduction in Cumulative Inpatient Days (RICID) and a reduction in inpatient admissions (Dietrich et al., 2017; Burns et al., 2007). This is a common outcome in ICM literature and is also a measure for reductions in healthcare costs, since inpatient treatments are bound to high costs.

In this study, there are mainly four groups of patients with SUDs that, despite previous or present linkages to health services, do need further or a different kind of treatment. Those patients are:

* People with low treatment satisfaction and high usage of health and social services: These patients, despite their previous treatments and social connections, do not improve sufficiently and continue to utilize healthcare services.
* people that already are in complex helping systems and make use of a high number of treatments but show a high need for coordination to be effective
* patients with dual diagnosis, with SUD being one of those in combination with, e.g., schizophrenia, personality disorders and anxiety disorders and would need intense and continuous care.
* people that, due to their clinical picture or other difficulties in life, do not have access to existing treatments (anymore) and fall through the social network. It includes people without permanent addresses, people with precarious housing conditions or socially isolated people, independent of their employment status.

Sex and gender will be treated as potential covariates and will be considered in the analysis.
primary_outcomes: Number of Inpatient Admissions (Health Service utilisation)
Number of Inpatient Days (Health Service utilisation)
title: Intensive Case Management for Substance Use Disorders (RCT)

brief_summary: In the aging population, ischemic heart disease, stroke and dementia are increasingly prevalent. Diagnosis and treatment of the former two i.e., large-vessel coronary heart disease and endovascular thrombectomy of the brain in relation to stroke have improved significantly. Yet, the majority of elderly patients with ischemic heart disease do not have large-vessel heart disease and it seems that small vessel disease (SVD) may explain a large fraction of these cases as well as the cardiovascular morbidity in the elderly. Hence, the current development in diagnostics and treatments of ischemic heart disease does not address the most common subtype of ischemic disease seen in elderly patients.It has been suggested that SVD is part of a multisystem disorder and several systematic reviews have addressed the hypothesis of a potential link between small vessel disease of the heart, brain, and kidneys. Cerebral SVD is prevalent in the aging population causing cognitive impairment, dementia, and an increased risk of stroke, and cerebral hypoperfusion is an acknowledged cause of vascular dementia and a possible cause of Alzheimer's disease. Further, cognitive impairment within multiple cognitive domains is highly prevalent in heart failure and is associated to an increased risk of dementia. The link between heart failure and dementia may be due to multisystem SVD, although a direct link between the two is possible.Among other known risk factors such as age, hypertension, and female sex, diabetes is a major cause of SVD and is linked to coronary heart disease as well as cognitive impairment. The diagnosis of cerebral SVD relies on MRI detecting infarctions, haemorrhages, microbleeds and ischemic white matter changes, i.e. Fazekas score. In contrast, perfusion PET is used to image myocardial perfusion in patients with coronary SVD; and coronary SVD is recognized as a part of the pathophysiology in angina, coronary artery disease, and heart failure. Perfusion PET before and after adenosine-induced vasodilation allows for measuring, the myocardial flow reserve (MFR), i.e. perfusion capacity, which in the absence of regional perfusion defects, is a measure of coronary SVD. Prof. Eva Prescott have recently shown that reduced MFR obtained by 82Rb PET is a strong predictor of future microvascular events and all-cause mortality.Exercise is well known to improve cognitive health but professor Carl-Johan Boraxbekk has shown that the effect on cognitive performance may be dependent on the initial cerebrovascular status, as patients with moderate to severe white matter changes did not improve after a 6 months physical activation intervention in contrast to patients with mild changes. Yet, it is possible to improve brain function in diabetic patients through either dietary or exercise interventions. Systemic SVD is measured as cerebral SVD (reduced brain perfusion during acetazolamide-induced vasodilation) and coronary SVD (reduced heart perfusion during adenosine-induced vasodilation). The researchers anticipate that patients with type 2 dabetes have reduced perfusion capacity of the brain and heart correlating to reduced cognition and cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2-max). Therefore we wish to see if we can improve both CBF and cognitive performance by improving VO2-max through a 16 week HIIT-training intervention.
primary_outcomes: [15O]H2O PET assessment of the blood perfusion to the brain
[15O]H2O PET assessment of the blood perfusion of the heart
title: The FIT-PET Study: Is Increased Cerebral Blood Flow a Mediator of the Beneficial Effects of HIIT-training on Cognitive Performance in Elderly Patients With Type 2 Diabetes?

brief_summary:
* The goal of this observational study is to learn whether frail older adults are more likely than older adults who are not frail to have low blood pressure after general anaesthesia starts and before surgery begins. The study includes adults aged 65 or older having planned surgery that is not heart surgery.
* Frailty means the body has less strength and reserve to cope with stress such as an operation. Low blood pressure is common in the first minutes of anaesthesia, and when it is deep or long it has been linked with kidney and heart problems after surgery. Earlier studies disagree on whether frail people are at higher risk.
* The researchers' hypothesis is that frail participants will have low blood pressure more often than participants who are not frail.
* The main question it aims to answer is: "Do frail participants have low blood pressure more often than participants who are not frail?"
* Low blood pressure means a mean arterial pressure (MAP), the average pressure in the arteries over one heartbeat, below 65 mmHg.
* About 400 people will take part at University Medical Center Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Before surgery, a trained researcher who does not take part in the person's anaesthesia care will rate frailty with the Clinical Frailty Scale, a 9-level scale based on daily activities; level 5 or higher counts as frail. Researchers will compare how often low blood pressure happens in frail and non-frail participants, allowing for age, other illnesses and blood pressure medicines. The researchers will also compare how low and how long blood pressure falls, the use of medicines to raise blood pressure, and kidney problems, confusion and hospital stay after surgery.

Participants will:

* Answer a few questions about daily life before surgery. A family member may help.
* Receive general anaesthesia with the drugs and doses this hospital uses as usual care.
* Have blood pressure checked every 2 minutes until surgery begins.
* Answer short questions about confusion on each of the first 3 days after surgery.

  * Low blood pressure is treated straight away. No extra blood is drawn, and participants may leave the study at any time without any effect on medical care. The results may help doctors know which older adults need closer blood pressure care when anaesthesia begins.
lead_sponsor: University Medical Center Ho Chi Minh City (UMC)
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with post-induction hypotension
title: Preoperative Frailty and Post-induction Hypotension in Older Adults Undergoing Elective Non-cardiac Surgery

brief_summary:
This is a Phase III, randomized, open-label, multicenter clinical study for patients with locally advanced, resectable head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC).

The current standard treatment for this disease includes surgery or radiation, but many patients still experience tumor recurrence or metastasis. This study aims to evaluate whether adding an immunotherapy drug (Camrelizumab) to standard chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel and cisplatin) before surgery or radiation can improve patient outcomes.

Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to one of two groups:

Experimental Group: Receives 3 cycles of Camrelizumab combined with nab-paclitaxel and cisplatin as neoadjuvant (pre-operative) therapy.

Control Group: Receives 3 cycles of nab-paclitaxel and cisplatin as neoadjuvant therapy.

After 3 cycles of treatment, doctors will evaluate the tumors. Depending on the tumor response, its location, and the patient's preference, participants will then receive either surgery (radical resection) or radiation therapy combined with cisplatin.

The main goal of this study is to compare the 2-year Event-Free Survival (EFS) between the two groups to see if the addition of Camrelizumab can prevent the disease from progressing or coming back. We will also monitor overall survival, organ preservation rates, and safety.
conditions: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancer
primary_outcomes: 2-year Event-Free Survival (EFS) Rate
title: Camrelizumab Plus Nab-Paclitaxel and Cisplatin Before Surgery for Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancer: a Randomized Phase III Trial

brief_summary:
Research shows 85% of the population will experience at least one episode of low back pain (LBP) in their lifetime. The annual cost to manage LBP in the U.S. can exceed 2 billion dollars. A conservative approach to LBP management can be provided by a physical therapist through interventions such as spinal mobilization. Spinal mobilizations are graded (I-IV) based upon the varying depths and impulse frequency at which they are applied to the target tissue. Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies have shown that spinal mobilizations (grade III, grade V) can stimulate pain suppression and provide favorable neurophysiological effects on pain modulation.

No studies to date, however, have examined the neurophysiological influence of grades II and IV on pain modulation. The purpose of this study is to investigate the change in pain suppression following spinal mobilization (i.e., grades II and IV).
interventions: Grade II central posterior-to-anterior spinal mobilization
Grade IV central posterior-to-anterior spinal mobilization
primary_outcomes: Numeric Pain Rating Scale
title: Impact of Spinal Mobilizations on Pain Modulation in People With Low Back Pain.

brief_summary:
European Association of Urology (EAU) guidelines mandate a second transurethral resection of bladder tumour (re-TURBt) for patients with high-grade or pT1 non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) to eradicate residual disease and avoid understaging. However, 30% to 50% or more of patients undergoing re-TURBt have no residual tumour found upon re-resection, incurring surgical and anaesthetic risks, potential morbidity, healthcare costs, and delays in adjuvant therapy without direct oncological benefit.

Current non-invasive triage tools, such as urine cytology and office cystoscopy, suffer from low sensitivity or diagnostic ambiguity due to ongoing post-operative inflammation and tissue healing in a recently resected bladder. While novel molecular biomarkers like Bladder EpiCheck® demonstrate high sensitivity and negative predictive value in the surveillance setting, single-timepoint measurements shortly after resection struggle to differentiate transient, healing-induced epigenetic changes from true persistent malignancy.

Evaluating the longitudinal trajectory of the EpiScore across two distinct post-operative timepoints (T1 and T2) provides a physiological basis for distinguishing decaying inflammatory/reparative signals from stable or rising signals indicative of residual disease. Demonstrating the diagnostic accuracy of Bladder EpiCheck® at T2, alongside the dynamic change in EpiScore (\ΔEpiScore), will establish whether non-invasive urine biomarker testing can reliably select low-risk pT1 NMIBC patients in whom re-TURBt can be safely omitted.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy of Bladder EpiCheck® test at timepoint T2 for residual disease at second TURBt in T1 NMIBC patients.
Diagnostic accuracy of change EpiScore between the two subsequent timepoints T1 and T2.
title: Urinary DNA Methylation Testing (Bladder EpiCheck®) and Its Peri-operative Kinetics for the Prediction of Residual Disease at Second Transurethral Resection in T1 Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial was to evaluate the effects of sequentially administrated physical activity and hypoxia on blood glucose, blood pressure and heart rate variability, compared to their isolated counterparts, in healthy individuals. The main question was to answer if this organization could be used as a beneficial modulator of metabolic and cardiovascular homeostasis without additional nervous autonomic strain.

Participants were asked to come for 5 visits at the laboratory for the following experimentations:

1. Inclusion visit with measurements of anthropometric data (height, weight, body composition), cardiorespiratory capacity (cycle ergometer sub-maximal incremental test) and strength of the upper and lower limbs (estimation the maximal repetition with a sub-maximal test).
2. Physical activity condition: 45 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise on a cycle ergometer (50-60% of the previously estimated maximal aerobic power) followed by 45 minutes of moderate resistance exercise (50-60% of the previously estimated maximal repetition).
3. Hypoxic condition: resting hypoxic exposure in a close environment with a 14.5% inspired oxygen fraction.
4. Sequential condition with a halved version of physical exercise (45 minutes) prior to hypoxic exposure (45 minutes).
5. Unsupervised control condition: measurement of the same outcomes in the daily living conditions.

Visits number 2, 3, 4, 5 were placed in random order.
interventions: Sequentially combined physical activity and hypoxia
primary_outcomes: Interstitial glucose concentrations
Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring
Heart rate variability
title: Effects of Physical Activity and Hypoxia on Blood Glucose, Blood Pressure and Heart Rate Variability in Healthy Individuals.

brief_summary:
The goal of this single-case experimental pilot study is to evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of an Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)-based individual intervention for adults with prolonged grief disorder.

Five adults aged 18 to 65 years with prolonged grief disorder are included in the study. The study uses a nonconcurrent multiple-baseline single-case experimental design. Participants complete repeated individualized daily assessments before, during, and after the intervention.

The intervention consists of eight weekly individual ACT sessions, each lasting approximately 45 to 60 minutes. Standardized measures of prolonged grief symptoms, psychological flexibility, and values-based living are administered before and immediately after the intervention. Follow-up assessments are also conducted 3 months after the final session, including standardized measures and 1 week of repeated individualized daily assessments.
interventions: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy-Based Individual Psychotherapy
primary_outcomes: Completion of the 8-Session Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Intervention
title: Living With Death: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for Prolonged Grief Disorder

brief_summary:
This study aimed to compare the effectiveness and safety of autologous platelet-rich plasma (A-PRP) injections and transobturator tape (TOT) surgery for treating stress urinary incontinence in women.

This prospective, randomized, parallel-group clinical trial included 80 women aged 18-65 years with confirmed stress urinary incontinence. Participants were randomly assigned to receive either A-PRP injections or TOT surgery, with 40 women in each group.

Participants were assessed before treatment and at 3 and 6 months after treatment. The primary outcome was the objective cure rate at 6 months, assessed using a standardized stress test. Secondary outcomes included urinary symptoms, quality of life, urine leakage, urodynamic measurements, adverse events, and the need for additional treatment.

The study was conducted at a tertiary-care academic institution in Egypt between June 2025 and June 2026.
primary_outcomes: Objective Cure Rate at 6 Months
title: Comparative Study Between Autologous Platelet Rich Plasma (A-PRP) Versus Trans Obturator Tape (TOT) for Treatment of Female Genuine Stress Urinary Incontinence (SUI)

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the feasibility and long-term efficacy of a 1-year hybrid rehabilitation program in adult patients with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1). DM1 is a progressive multisystemic disorder characterized by muscle wasting and weakness, which severely limits mobility and daily activities. Since disease-modifying pharmaceuticals are currently unavailable, interventions aimed at preserving or improving muscle function are critical.

This prospective, controlled pilot study evaluates an extended, year-long hybrid exercise protocol that combines intensive, supervised in-patient rehabilitation blocks with an intermediate, home-based training phase. The study tests the hypothesis that a long-term, structured exercise program is safe and can effectively preserve or improve functional gait capacity, muscle strength, and health-related quality of life in ambulatory DM1 patients compared to conventional care.
primary_outcomes: Six-Minute Walk Test (6MWT)
title: In-patient and Home-based Rehabilitation for Myotonic Dystrophy Patients

brief_summary:
The goal of this interventional study is to evaluate the effectiveness of a school-based program aimed at increasing mental health literacy in children aged 8 to 12 years, before implemention in French schools. The main question it aims to answer is: "How can we intervene to improve the mental health literacy of children aged 8 to 12?". The outcome measures are: 1) Change in children's mental health literacy score after the school-based intervention; and 2) Change in children's mental health literacy score after the intervention, according to the schools' geographical and socio-economic areas.

Through a mixed-methods approach, researchers will compare the score level of mental health literacy between an intervention and a control group of children with a quasi-experimental cluster trial. The intervention will last 6 weeks (one session of the program per week) during which a teacher and a child psychologist will present mental health according to the theoretical Child-focused Mental Health Literacy Model. Both groups will anser to a questionnaire including the CHILD-MHL scale on child mental health literacy. Additional interviews with teachers and in-class discussion with children will be performed.
primary_outcomes: Change in children's mental health literacy score after the school-based intervention.
title: Evaluation of a School Program Helping Children Understand Mental Health

brief_summary:
This retrospective observational study examines whether the number and location of involved lymph node stations before treatment help predict pathological response and survival in patients with resectable stage III N2 non-small cell lung cancer. The study includes 336 patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy combined with a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor at seven hospitals in China between January 2019 and January 2024. Patients who did not undergo planned surgery because of disease progression or serious adverse events remain in the cohort.

The nodal features are the number of distinct involved N1 and N2 stations, the individual stations involved, and the lung lobe or lobes containing the primary tumor. Each station is counted once. Statistical models will estimate lobe-specific higher-risk and lower-risk station patterns and the corresponding numbers of involved stations. These patterns are derived from the clinical data and are not assigned in advance according to presumed lymphatic drainage.

Primary outcomes are pathological complete response, major pathological response, event-free survival, and overall survival. The principal station-risk map is based on predicted 48-month event-free risk, with 36-month estimates as a supplementary analysis. Models based on clinical features, clinical features plus station counts, and additional lobe-specific station patterns will be compared using internal validation.

This is a separate secondary analysis that partly reuses participants from an earlier registered study and includes updated and additional data. Outcomes from the source cohort have already been examined. The registration documents the revised retrospective analysis and does not establish that its methods were specified before those outcomes were known. Treatment was selected by the treating clinicians, and this study assigns no treatment.
primary_outcomes: Pathological complete response (pCR)
Major pathological response (MPR)
Event-free survival (EFS)
Overall survival (OS)
title: Lymph Node Station Burden and Model-Derived Risk Patterns in N2 Lung Cancer After Neoadjuvant Chemoimmunotherapy

brief_summary:
The progression of small B-cell lymphomas toward a more aggressive histological form, specifically, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a serious and most often fatal event. This process gives rise to several categories of scientific challenges :

1. Anticipating this transformation through the early detection-while the disease is still in its indolent B-cell lymphoma stage-of biological markers that predict such a shift, particularly those that define tumor sub-clones at high risk of transformation.
2. Identifying the specific event(s) that, within an ongoing and continuous process, trigger the definitive transition from the indolent B-cell lymphoma phase to the transformed B-cell lymphoma phase.
3. Identifying the disrupted biological functions that drive treatment resistance in the transformed B-cell lymphoma stage, with the goal of defining new therapeutic targets.

Hypothesis :

1. The aggressive transformation of indolent B-cell lymphomas results from an imbalance in the subclonal structure, driven by the evolution of a dominant subclone that undergoes aggressive transformation. This subclonal competition-occurring either spontaneously or under therapeutic pressure-is fueled by the acquisition and/or selection of specific molecular and epigenetic alterations, as well as favorable remodeling of the tumor microenvironment. Some of these changes are detectable as early as the indolent phase, offering the prospect of early detection, while others dictate the mechanisms of therapeutic resistance following transformation.
2. Understanding the mechanisms of therapeutic resistance in transformed DLBCL could pave the way for the development of new, effective treatments. Furthermore, these insights could potentially be applied to resistant forms of de novo DLBCL-the most common category (40%) of B-cell lymphoma.

Our primary objective is to identify and validate the molecular, cellular, and microenvironmental alterations associated with therapeutic resistance in transformed B-cell lymphomas, and to investigate the presence of these mechanisms in resistant forms of de novo DLBCL.

Secondary objective 1. To understand the mechanisms underlying tumor evolution in each subtype of transformed B-cell lymphoma, with regard to both the characteristics of the tumor cell and its microenvironment.

Secondary objective 2. To develop cellular and animal models that mimic the transformed phase of indolent B-cell lymphomas.

Secondary objective 3. To identify biological characteristic, at the indolent B-cell lymphoma stag, that are predictive of aggressive transformation.
conditions: Transformed Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia to Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
Transformed Follic Lymph to Diff Large B-Cell Lymphoma
interventions: Identification of molecular and/or cellular signatures associated with the type of treatment response in patients with transformed B-cell lymphoma
Identify, at the indolent/small-cell B-cell lymphoma stage, the biological characteristics that are predictive of aggressive transformation.
investigate the existence of these mechanisms in resistant forms of de novo diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
primary_outcomes: To identify and validate the molecular, cellular, and microenvironmental alterations associated with therapeutic resistance in transformed B-cell lymphomas, and to investigate the presence of these mechanisms in resistant forms of *de novo* DLBCLs
title: Transformed B-cell Lymphoma : Clonal Evolution, Microenvironment Remodeling and Therapeutic Targets Discovery; Prospective Program
