brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of psychosocial skills training on psychological well-being and functioning in adults with psychotic disorders. People living with psychotic disorders may experience difficulties in communication, daily activities, social relationships, and maintaining psychological well-being. Psychosocial skills training is designed to help individuals develop practical skills for managing these challenges.

The study will include 34 adults diagnosed with psychotic or schizophrenia spectrum disorders who receive care at a community mental health center in Türkiye. Participants will be randomly assigned to an intervention group (17 participants) or a control group (17 participants).

The intervention group will receive eight weekly, face-to-face group sessions of psychosocial skills training (RUTBE), each lasting approximately 90-120 minutes. The sessions will address communication, problem-solving, understanding mental illness and its treatment, coping with symptoms, managing stress, and improving social and daily living skills. The control group will continue receiving routine care without the additional training during the study period.

Psychological well-being and functioning will be assessed in both groups before the training, immediately after the eight-session program, and three months later. The study will examine whether adding psychosocial skills training to routine mental health care improves psychological well-being and functioning compared with routine care alone.
primary_outcomes: Change in Psychological Well-Being Scale Score
Change in Functioning Assessment Short Test (FAST) Total Score
title: Effects of Psychosocial Skills Training on Well-Being and Functioning in People With Psychotic Disorders

brief_summary: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic condition that often imposes significant psychological distress and requires complex daily self-management. This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured nurse-led intervention combined with patient navigation on reducing psychological distress and improving self-management behaviors among patients with diabetes. Eligible adult patients with diabetes will be randomly assigned into either an intervention group receiving the nurse-led educational, psychosocial, and navigation support program alongside routine care, or a control group receiving routine diabetes care alone. Outcomes related to diabetes-related psychological distress and self-care adherence will be assessed at baseline and following the intervention period to determine the clinical impact of the program.
interventions: Nurse-Led Remote Monitoring and Patient Navigation
primary_outcomes: changes in psychological distress
Change in Diabetes Self-Management
title: Effect of Nurse-Led Remote Monitoring and Patient Navigation on Psychological Distress and Self-Management

brief_summary:
LATE syndrome (Limbic-predominant Age-related TDP-43 Encephalopathy) is a neurocognitive disorder associated with TDP-43 proteinopathy, whose clinical presentation-a hippocampal amnestic syndrome-is similar to that of Alzheimer's disease. There are no specific markers to differentiate between the two, other than the exclusion of Alzheimer's biomarkers (AB), a criterion limited by the possibility of comorbidity. In the era of anti-amyloid therapies, it is crucial to differentiate between them in order to appropriately offer these therapies to patients. The clinical diagnosis of LATE is therefore of great importance. A pattern specific to LATE has been described on PET-CT and may facilitate this diagnosis.

To study the concordance between the PET-CT pattern and the clinical criteria for LATE, we will compare changes in MMSE scores over one year between patients classified as "LATE" or "AD" based on 18F-FDG PET-CT.
primary_outcomes: MMSE score
title: CHUCOLATE: Current Knowledge and Prevalence of LATE-NC in Geriatric Memory Clinics at a Memory Center in Lorraine

brief_summary: FOLFOX-based hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) is widely used for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in China, yet many patients show primary resistance or progress after an initial response, and no prospective trial has defined the optimal salvage strategy. This single-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial evaluates the efficacy and safety of chemotherapy-minimized, blank microsphere-based transarterial chemoembolization (BMS-TACE) in patients with BCLC stage B/C HCC resistant to FOLFOX-HAIC. In BMS-TACE, blank microspheres are the principal embolic agent and chemotherapy is used only as an adjunct at a minimal dose (low-dose pirarubicin in a small volume of lipiodol), in order to limit chemotherapy-related liver injury and systemic toxicity and to allow repeated embolization in patients with limited hepatic reserve. Forty-three participants will be enrolled using a Simon two-stage design. The primary endpoint is objective response rate by investigator assessment using mRECIST.
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR) Per Modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST) as Assessed by Investigator
title: Chemotherapy-Minimized Blank Microsphere Transarterial Embolization (BMS-TACE) in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Resistant to FOLFOX-Based Hepatic Arterial Infusion Chemotherapy

brief_summary:
This pilot study aims to evaluate the safety and feasibility of epidural spinal cord stimulation (scES) combined with intensive rehabilitation in individuals with chronic spinal cord injury (SCI). The study will enroll up to 10 adults with spinal cord injury who are unable to walk independently in the community.

Participants will undergo surgical implantation of an epidural spinal cord stimulation system, followed by individualized stimulation programming and 80 sessions of activity-based rehabilitation focusing on voluntary lower extremity movements, standing, and stepping.

The primary objectives are to assess the safety of the implantation and stimulation procedures and the feasibility of implementing the rehabilitation protocol. Secondary objectives include evaluating potential changes in motor function, autonomic function, psychological well-being, and quality of life.

Participants will be followed for approximately 12 months, with repeated clinical and functional assessments throughout the study.
primary_outcomes: Serious Adverse Events
Participant Recruitment Rate
Retention at 6 Months
Retention at 12 Months
Stimulation Mapping
Number of Rehabilitation Training Sessions Completed
title: Epidural Spinal Cord Stimulation for Motor Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury: A Pilot Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if adding platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections near the clitoris improves sexual function more than PRP injections in the vaginal wall alone. The study includes sexually active adults who were assigned female at birth. PRP is made from a person's own blood. It contains growth factors that may help tissue heal and renew.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does adding PRP near the clitoris improve sexual function 6 weeks after treatment, compared with vaginal wall PRP alone? Do any improvements last at 3 and 6 months? How painful are the injections, and what side effects do participants have?

Researchers will compare two groups. All participants will get PRP injected into the front wall of the vagina. One group will also get PRP injected near the clitoris. The other group will get a placebo (sham) injection near the clitoris: the needle goes under the skin, but nothing is injected. Participants will not know which group they are in.

Participants will:

Answer questionnaires about their health and sexual function before treatment. Come to one in-person visit, about 1 hour long. At this visit they will have blood drawn to make the PRP and receive the injections.

Rate their pain shortly after the injections. Complete 3 short online follow-up visits at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months. At these visits they will answer questionnaires about sexual function and side effects.
primary_outcomes: Change in Female Sexual Function Index Total Score
title: Sexual Function Outcomes Following Peri-clitoral PRP

brief_summary: This prospective observational study aims to evaluate the agreement between the non-invasive Pleth Variability Index (PVi) and manually calculated invasive Pulse Pressure Variation (PPV) during gynecological laparoscopic surgery. Measurements will be obtained at five predefined intraoperative time points corresponding to baseline supine positioning, pneumoperitoneum, 15-degree Trendelenburg positioning, 30-degree Trendelenburg positioning, and return to the supine position after desufflation. The study will assess changes in the relationship and agreement between these two hemodynamic parameters under different surgical conditions.
primary_outcomes: Agreement Between Pleth Variability Index (PVi) and Manually Calculated Invasive Pulse Pressure Variation (PPV)
title: Agreement Between Pleth Variability Index and Arterial Pulse Pressure Variation During Gynecological Laparoscopic Surgery

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-center observational cohort study aims to investigate the development of anti-Adalimumab antibodies in pediatric patients with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and/or chronic non-infectious uveitis initiating Adalimumab treatment.

The study will assess the frequency and timing of antibody development, identify potential predictive factors, including concomitant methotrexate treatment, and explore associations between immunogenicity, serum Adalimumab concentrations, disease activity, and clinical outcomes.

A total of 60 patients will be enrolled and followed for 24 months. Clinical data and additional blood samples will be collected at baseline and at 3, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months during routine clinical visits.

Anti-Adalimumab antibodies and serum drug concentrations will be measured using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) technology. Treatment decisions will remain entirely based on routine clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Patients Developing Anti-Adalimumab Antibodies
Time to Development of Anti-Adalimumab Antibodies
title: Anti-Adalimumab Antibodies in Children With Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis and/or Chronic Non-Infectious Uveitis

primary_outcomes: Safe Dose Level (Recommended Phase 2 Dose)
title: Determining the Safety of CAR T-Cell Therapy for Lymphoma

Changes in V02 using indirect calorimetry at baseline and following the intervention.

The study will be split into two parts, Part A and Part B.

The study is looking at:

* What side effects REGN20566 might cause
* How much REGN20566 is in the blood at different times
* If the body reacts to REGN20566 in a way that may cause REGN20566 to not work as well

Occurrence of TEAEs

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study was to find out whether kinesio taping applied to the abdominal muscles changes balance, trunk position sense, trunk muscle endurance, flexibility and agility in young male football players, compared with sham taping.

Thirty-six male football players aged 16 to 19 years from a professional club academy were randomly assigned to kinesio taping or sham taping. All tests were performed before taping and 45 minutes after taping in a single session.
primary_outcomes: Dynamic balance (Y Balance Test reach distance)

brief_summary: This study aims to find out whether an ultrasound-guided deep rectus sheath block, a regional anesthesia technique that numbs the nerves of the front abdominal wall, reduces pain and the need for opioid pain medication after laparoscopic radical prostatectomy. Adult men scheduled for elective laparoscopic radical prostatectomy will be randomly assigned to receive either a bilateral deep rectus sheath block with the local anesthetic bupivacaine or a sham (placebo) block with saline, performed after induction of general anesthesia. Patients and the clinicians caring for and assessing them will not know which treatment was given. All patients will receive the same general anesthesia and the same pain-relief protocol, including intravenous tramadol by patient-controlled analgesia (PCA). The main question is whether the block reduces the amount of tramadol used in the first 24 hours after surgery. Pain scores, rescue pain medication, opioid-related side effects and quality of recovery will also be compared.
interventions: Ultrasound-guided bilateral deep rectus sheath block
lead_sponsor: Marmara University Pendik Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Cumulative 24-hour intravenous tramadol consumption via patient-controlled analgesia
title: Deep Rectus Sheath Block for Postoperative Pain in Laparoscopic Radical Prostatectomy

title: Peds Proton Therapy

brief_summary: This research is planned to determine the effect of an AI-assisted nursing diagnostic system on nurses' perceptions of diagnoses, their opinions regarding diagnoses, and their attitudes towards artificial intelligence. The research will be conducted using a randomized controlled experimental design with an AI-assisted nursing diagnostic system developed for the field of women's health and obstetrics. The study population consists of nurses working in the obstetrics and gynecology departments (delivery room, postpartum ward, etc.) of two hospitals and providing care to women aged 18-49. Approximately 600 nurses meeting the inclusion criteria were identified as constituting the population. In the study, nurses' perceptions of diagnoses, their opinions regarding nursing diagnoses, and their attitudes towards artificial intelligence will be evaluated through structured data collection tools. The use of the AI-assisted system will be compared with traditional nursing diagnostic processes to analyze the system's impact on clinical decision-making processes. The study expects that the AI-assisted nursing diagnostic system will increase diagnostic accuracy, support clinical decision-making processes, and positively influence nurses' attitudes towards technology. Furthermore, it is anticipated that the findings will contribute to the standardization of nursing care and provide a scientific basis for the development of digital health applications aimed at improving maternal and infant safety in the field of women's health.
interventions: Implementation of an AI-supported mobile application for nurses
primary_outcomes: Nursing Diagnosis Perception Scale
Scale of Opinions on Nursing Diagnoses
Artificial Intelligence Attitude Scale for Nurses
Development of an Artificial Intelligence and NANDA-NIC-NOC (NNN) Ontology-Based Mobile Decision Support System
title: THE EFFECT OF AI-SUPPORTED WOMEN'S HEALTH NURSING DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS ON NURSES' DIAGNOSTIC PERCEPTIONS AND AI ATTITUDES

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, uncontrolled pilot study evaluating changes in plasma LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) concentrations before and after 3 months of intake of the dietary supplement LIPI-PROTECT-2.The main objective of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effect of LIPI-PROTECT-2 on plasma LDL-C concentration after 3 months of supplementation in participants with untreated moderate hypercholesterolemia.A mean reduction in plasma LDL-C levels of approximately 14% (0.20 g/L) is expected after 3 months of supplementation.The primary endpoint is the absolute (g/L) and relative (%) change in plasma LDL-C concentration between baseline and Month 3.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the effect of LIPI-PROTECT-2 on plasma LDL-cholesterol concentration (absolute value) after 3 months of consumption in subjects with untreated moderate hypercholesterolemia
title: LIPI- PROTECT-2 : Dietary Supplement in Subjects With Moderate Hypercholesterolemia (LPP2)

brief_summary:
This study aimed to investigate the frequency and patterns of lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) and evaluate changes in urinary symptoms during a structured 12-week Kegel exercise programme.

This prospective, single-arm, non-randomised interventional study was conducted at Shaikh Zayed Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan, between June and September 2026. A total of 100 patients with Parkinson's disease, aged 40-80 years, underwent baseline assessment. Of these, 66 participants with urinary symptoms entered a 12-week Kegel exercise programme, while 34 participants without urinary symptoms underwent baseline assessment only.

Participants receiving the intervention were instructed to perform 45 pelvic floor muscle contractions daily, divided into three sets of 15 contractions. Follow-up assessments were conducted at Weeks 6 and 12.

Urinary symptoms and associated quality-of-life outcomes were evaluated using the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Overactive Bladder (ICIQ-OAB), urinary quality-of-life questionnaires, and three-day bladder diaries. Exercise adherence and patient-reported improvement were also assessed.

The study aimed to characterise urinary symptom patterns in Parkinson's disease and describe changes observed during the Kegel exercise programme. Because the study did not include a control group, it was not designed to establish a causal treatment effect.
lead_sponsor: Sheikh Zayed Federal Postgraduate Medical Institute
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms
title: Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Parkinson's Disease and Changes During Kegel Exercises

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to investigate the prevalence of iron deficiency and the association to psychiatric symptoms in girls 15-18 years attending adolescent mental health services and for those who have an iron deficit offer three months of iron supplementation to evaluate the effect on iron status and on psychiatric symptoms.

THE MAIN QUESTIONS THE STUDY AIMS TO ANSWER IS:

1. How prevalent is iron deficiency in girls age 15-18 years in adolescent mental health?
2. Is iron deficiency associated to psychiatric symptoms?
3. Does iron supplementation with SiderAL- forte, a mild nutritional supplement, improve iron stores and psychiatric symptoms? Is the supplementation well tolerated?
4. Qualitatively: How do participants describe their understanding of well-being and regarding being informed of low iron stores?How do participants experience iron supplementation and factors that hinder or facilitate treatment?

WHAT IS THE ACTIVITY FOR THE PARTICIPANT?

* The ongoing treatment at the service is not affected.
* Blood sampling at the local clinic or with the general practioner and online self report forms are collected at baseline.
* Participants with iron deficiency will be offered iron supplementation with SiderAL- forte, a mild nutritional supplement for three months.
* Blood sampling and online self report forms will be collected at 3 and 6 months after start of iron supplementation.
primary_outcomes: The PROMIS paediatric fatigue scale
title: Non-anaemic Iron Deficiency and Iron Supplementation in Girls 15-18 Yrs

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of a 12-week (24-session) structured myofascial training program on regional crural fascia thickness and vertical jump performance in healthy high school adolescents. Fifty-three adolescents (mean age \~14.2 years) were randomly allocated to either a myofascial training group or a habitual physical activity control group. Crural fascia thickness was evaluated via B-mode ultrasonography at eight anatomical regions across the anterior, lateral, and posterior leg compartments at baseline, week 4, week 8, and week 12. Countermovement jump (CMJ) and squat jump (SJ) kinetic and kinematic parameters were assessed on a dual force platform before and after the 12-week intervention.
primary_outcomes: Crural Fascia Thickness
Countermovement Jump (CMJ) Height
Squat Jump
title: Effects of a 12-Week Myofascial Training Program on Crural Fascia Thickness and Jump Performance in Adolescents: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Type 2 diabetes is a long-term condition that requires patients to manage their diet, physical activity, medication, and blood glucose levels regularly. Diabetes self-management education can help patients improve their knowledge and daily self-care practices. However, educational programs may be more effective when they consider patients' local culture, language, food habits, and family values.

This study evaluated the effectiveness of a culturally based Diabetes Self-Management Education (DSME) model among adults with type 2 diabetes in Bone Regency, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. The study involved participants from Puskesmas Cina and used a quasi-experimental design with intervention and control groups.

Participants in the intervention group received general counselling supported by a culturally based DSME module developed for the Bugis community. The module covered basic diabetes knowledge, nutrition using locally available foods, physical activity, blood glucose monitoring, foot care, stress management, and family support. The education was delivered in four group sessions, once a week for four consecutive weeks. Participants in the control group received general diabetes counselling without the culturally based module.

The study assessed quality of life, diabetes knowledge, self-management practices, and blood glucose levels. Fasting blood glucose and two-hour post-meal blood glucose were monitored over 12 weeks. Quality of life, knowledge, and self-management were assessed before the intervention and at three months.

The purpose of this study was to determine whether culturally based diabetes education could improve quality of life, diabetes self-management, and blood glucose control compared with general diabetes counselling.
primary_outcomes: Quality of Life Measured by WHOQOL-BREF
title: Culturally Based Diabetes Self-Management Education for Adults With Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary: This study was conducted to evaluate the effect of initial periodontal treatment on clinical parameters, gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) volume, cotinine levels and tissue factor (TF) activity in saliva and GCF in smoker and non-smoker patients with chronic periodontitis. Forty systemically healthy patients with chronic periodontitis (20 smokers, 20 non-smokers) were included. Initial periodontal treatment consisting of oral hygiene instruction, scaling and root planing was applied. Clinical measurements were recorded and saliva and GCF samples were collected at baseline and 1 and 3 months after treatment.

Participants with a severely resorbed upper jaw will receive four dental implants placed according to the All-on-4 protocol. Each participant will sequentially wear three different prosthetic designs over defined follow-up periods. At the end of each period, patient satisfaction will be assessed using standardized questionnaires, and any mechanical or prosthetic complications will be recorded and compared among the three prosthetic designs.

brief_summary:
This study will compare two fresh gas flow rates during general anesthesia in adults undergoing lumbar stabilization surgery while lying face down. Fresh gas flow is the rate at which oxygen and other gases are supplied to the anesthesia breathing system. Lower flow rates may reduce anesthetic use and its environmental impact, but their effects on breathing during prolonged surgery need further evaluation.

Seventy adults will be randomly assigned to receive a fresh gas flow rate of either 0.3 or 2 liters per minute. Both groups will receive sevoflurane anesthesia and standardized mechanical ventilation.

The main outcome is the percentage change in dynamic respiratory system compliance, a measure of how easily the lungs and chest expand during ventilation, between 10 and 120 minutes after reaching the assigned flow rate. Other assessments will include breathing mechanics, blood oxygen and carbon dioxide levels, brain oxygenation, lung ultrasound findings, postoperative oxygen needs, pulmonary complications, and hospital length of stay. Anesthetic and fresh gas consumption, anesthetic cost, and estimated greenhouse gas emissions will also be compared. Fresh gas flow will be increased if predefined safety criteria are met.
interventions: Minimal Fresh Gas Flow at 0.3 L/min
primary_outcomes: Percentage Change in Dynamic Respiratory System Compliance
title: Effects of Two Fresh Gas Flow Rates During Anesthesia for Lumbar Stabilization Surgery

brief_summary: Hyperkalemia is a common and potentially fatal electrolyte disorder in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis, but it is currently detected only by periodic blood tests. This prospective, single-center observational cohort study will evaluate whether T-wave morphology measured with a six-channel wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) patch can identify hyperkalemia (serum potassium greater than 5.0 mEq/L) in these patients. Forty adults on thrice-weekly hemodialysis will wear the device during one dialysis session per month for 6 months. ECG recordings will be compared with serum potassium measured before and after the same dialysis session. No treatment is assigned by the study, and no additional blood draws are required.
primary_outcomes: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of the pre-dialysis T-wave morphology index for discriminating hyperkalemia
title: Six-Channel Wearable ECG for Prediction of Hyperkalemia in Hemodialysis Patients

brief_summary: Pharyngocutaneous fistula (PCF) is one of the most feared complications after total laryngectomy. A compressive neck dressing is often applied after surgery to try to prevent it, but there is no consensus on whether it works or how long it should be kept, and practice varies widely between centers. This multicenter, retrospective, observational study compares the rate of PCF in adult patients with laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma who underwent primary total laryngectomy with direct closure of the hypopharyngeal mucosa and who did or did not receive a postoperative compressive dressing. It also examines whether the duration of the dressing affects the risk of fistula and how fistulas were managed in the two groups. All data are collected from existing medical records; no additional treatment or examination is performed.
conditions: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Larynx
primary_outcomes: Incidence of pharyngocutaneous fistula
title: Compressive Dressing and Pharyngocutaneous Fistula After Primary Total Laryngectomy

To the best of our knowledge, no studies have specifically evaluated prophylactic vasopressor use in patients undergoing emergency surgery for septic source control. In this study, we investigate the efficacy of titrated norepinephrine infusion as a prophylactic strategy against intraoperative hypotension in emergency surgery.

title: Titrated Norepinephrine for Prophylaxis Against Intraoperative Hypotension in Emergency Surgery

brief_summary: The primary objective of this prospective clinical study is to evaluate the incidence of hemidiaphragmatic paralysis when the phrenic nerve is utilized as a primary sonographic landmark during interscalene brachial plexus blocks. While interscalene blocks provide excellent analgesia for shoulder surgeries, they are frequently associated with unintended phrenic nerve blockade, leading to diaphragmatic paresis or paralysis. This study hypothesizes that utilizing the phrenic nerve as a specific landmark to guide local anesthetic injection will \[reduce\] the frequency of diaphragmatic paralysis while maintaining adequate surgical anesthesia.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Transient Hemidiaphragmatic Paralysis

brief_summary:
In France, the number of new cancer cases across all cancer types was estimated at 382,000 in 2018. The impact of pain on a patient's quality of life is profound, with physical consequences (insomnia, fatigue, loss of appetite), psychological effects (anxiety, depression, demoralization, attention deficit, memory disorders), and social repercussions.

Acute pain induced by cancer, when poorly managed, can lead to the development of secondary chronic pain syndrome. The French National Authority for Health (Haute Autorité de Santé, HAS) deplores the late referral of patients with chronic pain, which complicates treatment and limits opportunities for improvement. Cancer-related pain has become a chronic condition in 50% of patients, leading to anxiety-depressive syndromes as well as social consequences such as social isolation or difficulty returning to professional activity.

In France, the 2017 White Paper by the SFETD (French Society for the Study and Treatment of Pain) notes that, despite three successive Cancer Plans integrating supportive care into the comprehensive management of cancer patients, one in three patients does not receive analgesic treatment appropriate to the intensity of their pain. To prevent chronic pain, the HAS recently recommended early assessment of acute pain (within less than a week) with a high-quality city-hospital organization.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of eligible patients that provide a consent to participate
Proportion of general pactitioner that confirmed their participation
Proportion of consultations with the general practitioner performed
Proportion of consultations at the hospital performed
title: Evaluation of a City-hospital Pathway for Early Management of Acute Pain in Oncology

brief_summary:
ADHD is one of the most common mental health conditions in teenagers. It can affect school performance, friendships, and overall well-being. Some everyday habits and lifestyle factors-how much a teenager plays internet games, how well they sleep, and whether they take part in sports-have each been linked to ADHD symptoms. However, these three factors have almost always been studied one at a time, and no study has yet tested whether looking at them together can help predict which teenagers have more severe ADHD symptoms.

This study aims to find out whether internet gaming, sleep quality, and sport participation, when considered together, can predict ADHD symptom severity in adolescents aged 12-17. We will invite 750 teenagers from secondary schools in Malatya, Türkiye, to complete a set of short, anonymous questionnaires about their attention and hyperactivity symptoms, gaming habits, sleep, and sport participation. We will then use machine learning-a type of computer analysis that can detect complex patterns and interactions between many factors at once-to build and test a prediction model.

The main question this study seeks to answer is: Do internet gaming, sleep quality, and sport participation jointly carry information that helps predict ADHD symptoms in teenagers, beyond what is already known from basic characteristics such as age, sex, and socioeconomic status? We are not testing a treatment, and the study does not involve any medication, biological samples, or changes to participants' usual routines. The findings may help schools, families, and health professionals identify teenagers who could benefit from early support and from healthier lifestyle habits. This is an exploratory study; it cannot show cause and effect, and any prediction model would need to be tested in other groups before being used in practice.
primary_outcomes: ADHD Symptom Severity: Conners-Wells Adolescent Self-Report Scale (CASS) Inattention and Hyperactivity Subscales
title: Machine Learning Prediction of ADHD in Adolescents: Gaming, Sleep, and Sport

brief_summary:
This is a monocenter, prospective cohort study. The study investigates the response of patients living with multiple sclerosis (MS) to vaccination against tick-borne viral encephalitis (TBE).

The prevalence of TBE has increased significantly in Switzerland over the past two decades. Whereas previously only the lowland regions of northern Switzerland and the Aare Valley were considered areas where TBE vaccination was indicated, the disease is now endemic throughout Switzerland (except for Ticino). Since TBE specifically affects the nervous system, there is a clear indication for vaccination, particularly for people whose nervous system is already compromised.

MS is the most common neurological autoimmune disease among young adults in northern latitudes. It is a progressive disease characterized by a gradual deterioration of neurological functions. The course of the disease can be slowed through immunomodulatory therapies. However, these therapies also lead to a certain degree of immunosuppression, which may reduce the immune response to vaccinations. At the same time, some people with MS experience fear or scepticism towards vaccinations, as infections often lead to a worsening of symptoms or can trigger a relapse. Since vaccinations mimic an infection to some extent, this concern is sometimes transferred to vaccinations as well.

The study hypothesizes that the TBE vaccine in people living with MS on non-B-cell depleting treatment shows adequate immunogenicity.

Moreover, the study will assess the safety of TBE vaccination.
lead_sponsor: Insel Gruppe AG, University Hospital Bern
primary_outcomes: Primary immunogenicity endpoint
title: Immunogenicity and Safety of Vaccination Against Tick Borne Encephalitis (TBE) in Patients Living With Multiple Sclerosis (MS)

brief_summary:
Urinary tract infections are common in infants, but obtaining a reliable urine sample from babies younger than 6 months can be challenging. Bladder catheterization is a commonly used method for collecting urine, although it is an invasive procedure that may cause discomfort.

This randomized, controlled, open-label clinical trial will compare two methods of urine collection in infants younger than 6 months of age who are suspected of having a urinary tract infection and require a urine test. The study will be conducted at Toledo University Hospital in Spain.

Infants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. The intervention group will undergo the Herreros technique, a non-invasive method that uses gentle tapping over the lower abdomen and circular massage of the lower back to stimulate spontaneous urination. The control group will undergo intermittent bladder catheterization to collect a urine sample.

The main objective is to compare the success of the two methods in obtaining a urine sample. Secondary objectives include comparing the time required to collect urine, sample contamination rates, pain or discomfort experienced by the infants, complications, costs, and parents' or legal guardians' satisfaction with the procedure.

The study aims to provide evidence on the effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness of the Herreros technique compared with bladder catheterization in infants younger than 6 months.
primary_outcomes: Successful urine sample collection rate
title: Effectiveness of the Herreros Urination Stimulation Technique Versus Bladder Catheterization for Urine Sample Collection in Infants Under 6 Months

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to develop practical, expert-agreed standards for nutrition care of critically ill adults in intensive care units (ICUs) in resource-limited settings. The main question it aims to answer is:

Which nutrition practices do international ICU experts agree are essential and achievable for critically ill patients in hospitals with limited resources?

Participants will be ICU doctors, dietitians and nurses with experience of nutrition care in resource-limited settings. They will rate a set of statements across five areas of ICU nutrition in anonymous online survey rounds. After each round they will see a summary of the group's responses and may revise their ratings. A statement reaches agreement when at least 80% of experts agree with it, and rounds will continue until responses stabilise. ICU survivors and family members will also review a plain-language version of the statements, and their feedback will be shared with the expert panel.
conditions: ICU Nutrition in Resource Limited Settings
primary_outcomes: To establish consensus-based minimum standards for assessment, initiation, delivery, and monitoring of nutritional therapy in resource-limited ICUs.
title: Expert Consensus on Nutrition Standards for Intensive Care Units in Resource Limited Settings

brief_summary:
The Investigators have demonstrated in preclinical studies that RNA liposomes activate APCs, induce antigen-specific T cell immunity, and can supplant DCs in a cell therapy model for HGG and have shown feasibility and activity of this approach in preclinical models and in canine patients with a spontaneous malignant glioma. In one arm of this study, we will investigate the safety and immunologic activity of RNA-LP vaccines in pediatric patients with recurrent pHGG.

The investigators have also shown that intravenous administration of tumor mRNA loaded lipid particles (LPs) localizes primarily to lung, transfect antigen presenting cells (APCs) and lead to an activated T cell response for induction of anti-tumor immunity. In contrast to other formulations, RNA-LPs recruit multiple arms of the immune system (i.e. innate/adaptive), and remodel the systemic/intratumoral immune milieu, which remain potent barriers for vaccine, cellular, and checkpoint inhibiting immunotherapies. After only a single RNA-LP vaccine, the bulk of systemic and intratumoral dendritic cells (DCs) in mice display an activated phenotype; these activated DCs (harvested from tumors) expand antigen specific T cell immunity. In immunologically resistant pulmonary osteosacroma murine tumor models (i.e. K7M2), RNA-LPs induce robust anti-tumor efficacy in settings where immune checkpoint inhibitors (i.e. anti-PD-L1 therapy) do not confer therapeutic benefit. The investigators have already demonstrated safety of RNA-LPs in acute/chronic murine toxicity studies, and in client-owned canine trial.

In this study, we will investigate the manufacturing feasibility, safety and immunologic activity of RNA-LP vaccine in patients with recurrent pulmonary or unresectable osteosarcoma and recurrent pHGG.
primary_outcomes: Maximum tolerated dose
Feasibility of generating RNA-LP
title: RNA Lipid Particles Targeting Pediatric Recurrent Intracranial Malignancies and Other systEmic Solid Tumors - High Grade Glioma

brief_summary: This single-center, prospective observational study will enroll 80 adults: 15 healthy controls, 20 participants with chronic hepatitis B, 20 participants with HBV-related cirrhosis, and 25 participants with HBV-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF). The study will not assign any research treatment, and all participants will continue to receive routine clinical care. A 5 mL peripheral blood sample will be collected once from the first three groups. Participants with HBV-ACLF will have 5 mL blood collected at baseline, Day 28, and Day 90, and their 28-day and 90-day survival status will be recorded. Plasma IL-33, IL-6, TNF-alpha, and IL-10 will be measured. Peripheral blood CD14-positive monocytes will be isolated, and ACOD1 and MARCO mRNA expression will be measured by quantitative PCR. The study will compare these markers across groups and assess their relationships with inflammation, disease severity, longitudinal clinical changes, and short-term outcomes.

brief_summary: Headaches in pediatric patients can be related to primary (essential) and secondary (symptomatic) causes. This study investigates the correlation between nasal dysfunction, specifically mucociliary clearance impairment and structural anomalies, and cephalalgia in children, with a focus on allergic rhinitis and rhinopathy. A total of 2,262 children aged 5 to 10 years were screened. Clinical evaluation included evaluation of headache history, nasal patency, mucociliary clearance function, and the presence of structural anomalies such as septal deviation or adenoidal hypertrophy. A significant association was found between nasal dysfunction and headache. Children with impaired mucociliary clearance, nasal obstruction, or structural abnormalities demonstrated a higher prevalence of cephalalgia compared to those with normal nasal function. Allergic rhinitis was frequently observed among patients who reported recurrent headaches. Altered nasal dysfunction appears to be an important and potentially underrecognized contributor to pediatric headache. These findings highlight the need for comprehensive Ear Nose Throat evaluation in children with recurrent and unexplained cephalalgia.

primary_outcomes: nasal airway conductance
title: Headache and Nasal Dysfunction in Children

Participants will receive 3-4 intravenous treatments, generally every 8 weeks, at an activity not exceeding 7.4 GBq per treatment, with amino acids for kidney protection. Side effects, blood counts, liver and kidney function, and treatment completion will be assessed. Tumor response, disease progression, and quality of life will also be evaluated. brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate and compare the effectiveness and safety of topical metformin 30% and topical minoxidil 5% in patients with alopecia areata.

Alopecia areata is an autoimmune condition that causes non-scarring hair loss, usually presenting as round or oval patches on the scalp. Different topical treatments are used to stimulate hair regrowth, but their effectiveness varies.

In this comparative interventional study, eligible patients with alopecia areata will receive either topical metformin 30% or topical minoxidil 5%. Treatment response will be assessed clinically during follow-up using standardized assessment methods, including the Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) score, along with clinical and dermoscopic evaluation.

The study aims to determine whether topical metformin 30% is an effective treatment option compared with topical minoxidil 5% in patients with alopecia
primary_outcomes: Change in SALT Score from Baseline to Week 12

brief_summary:
LCCC 2534-ATL is an early-stage (Phase 1), single-center clinical study evaluating the safety of CAR T-cell therapy in children and adults with high-grade gliomas (HGGs), which are aggressive brain cancers.

The treatment, called iC9-CAR.B7-H3 T cells, uses modified immune cells designed to recognize and attack cancer cells with a protein called B7-H3. The treatment also includes a safety switch (iC9) designed to help stop the modified cells if serious side effects occur.

Earlier studies of B7-H3-targeted CAR T-cell therapy have shown encouraging safety results, with some patients experiencing tumor shrinkage. This study will further evaluate the safety and tolerability of the treatment in children and adults with high-grade gliomas type brain tumors.

The study will use a 3+3 dose-escalation design to evaluate increasing doses and identify the safest appropriate dose. The results will help determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D), which is the dose selected for further study.

Participants who qualify will have blood collected to produce the modified T cells. Three treatment doses will be administered two weeks apart. Additional doses may be given.

Participants will be monitored for 15 years after treatment ends or is discontinued to assess potential long-term side effects related to genetic modification of the cells.

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a cream containing tretinoin and tranexamic acid compared with tretinoin cream alone in managing post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation following electrosurgery in patients with benign skin tumors. Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation is a condition in which the skin becomes darker after inflammation or injury, including after certain dermatological procedures. This discoloration may affect patients' appearance and quality of life.

The study will compare two treatment groups: one receiving a combination of tretinoin and tranexamic acid cream and the other receiving tretinoin cream alone. Participants will undergo treatment for four weeks. The researchers will evaluate changes in skin pigmentation and skin barrier function using the Post-Inflammatory Hyperpigmentation Area and Severity Index (PIHASI), transepidermal water loss (TEWL), and skin hydration measurements.

The findings are expected to provide information about the potential benefits of combining tretinoin and tranexamic acid for managing hyperpigmentation after electrosurgery.

brief_summary:
This study examined how often, how long, and at what level of effort people should practice getting out of bed and moving during their hospital stay after an ischemic stroke. Early mobilization included activities such as sitting at the edge of the bed, standing, moving from the bed to a chair, and walking with help as needed.

In the first stage, 63 participants were randomly assigned to one of nine early mobilization programs that differed in the number of daily sessions, the length of each session, and the level of effort. The researchers used information on recovery, safety, and how much of each program could be delivered to select two programs for further study.

In the second stage, a separate group of 60 participants was randomly assigned to one of the two selected programs or to a comparison program consisting of one 10-minute session of low-intensity mobilization each day. All participants received routine hospital rehabilitation in addition to their assigned program. The study tested whether the selected programs improved how independently participants could carry out daily activities three months after stroke.
primary_outcomes: Modified Rankin Scale
title: Optimization of Early Mobilization

brief_summary:
Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a serious and potentially life-threatening complication of type 1 diabetes. Adolescents with type 1 diabetes need to perform daily self-management activities, such as taking insulin as prescribed, monitoring blood glucose levels, managing food intake, checking ketones when indicated, and responding appropriately to illness or abnormal blood glucose levels. However, maintaining these behaviors can be challenging during adolescence.

This study aims to evaluate the effect of a self-efficacy promoting program delivered through a LINE Bot (SE-LINE) on self-management behaviors to prevent diabetic ketoacidosis among adolescents with type 1 diabetes.

The program uses the LINE messaging application to provide educational information and learning activities designed to strengthen adolescents' confidence in their ability to manage diabetes. The program is based on the concept of self-efficacy and aims to support adolescents in developing the knowledge, confidence, and practical skills needed to perform appropriate diabetes self-management behaviors.

The study will assess changes in self-management behaviors related to DKA prevention before and after participation in the program. The findings may provide evidence on the use of a digital communication platform to support diabetes self-management among adolescents and inform the development of accessible nursing interventions for preventing DKA in this population.
primary_outcomes: Self-Management Behaviors for Diabetic Ketoacidosis Prevention
title: A LINE Bot-Based Self-Efficacy Program to Improve Self-Management and Prevent Diabetic Ketoacidosis in Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes

brief_summary: The REMEDE study, a single-center retrospective and prospective observational study conducted at the Fondazione Policlinico Universitario Agostino Gemelli IRCCS, aims to evaluate the validity of laparoscopic intraoperative ultrasound (IOUS) in measuring rectosigmoid deep infiltrating endometriosis nodules. The primary objective is to determine the equivalence and agreement between nodule dimensions (expressed in millimeters) measured via postoperative histological examination-considered the gold standard-preoperative transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS), and laparoscopic intraoperative ultrasound performed after bowel mobilization (IOUS). Secondary objectives include analyzing potential systematic bias (overestimation or underestimation) of the ultrasound methods compared to histology, evaluating direct agreement between TVUS and IOUS, and conducting an exploratory analysis to verify whether factors such as lesion location, presence of adhesions, and nodule size influence measurement accuracy. The study plans to enroll a total of 20 adult female patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery for posterior compartment endometriosis with rectosigmoid involvement. The primary endpoint will be statistically analyzed using the Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) approach to test the equivalence of paired differences based on predefined margins, supported by descriptive analyses using the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman methods.
lead_sponsor: Fondazione Policlinico Universitario Agostino Gemelli IRCCS
primary_outcomes: Equivalence between rectosigmoid endometriosis nodule dimensions.
title: Validation Study of Laparoscopic Intraoperative Ultrasound for Measuring Rectosigmoid Deep Infiltrating Endometriosis Nodules
